detail.abstract: How do state taxes respond to changes in oil prices? For the United States, the answer remains inconclusive. We use a consumer optimization model to derive an optimal tax function, whose parameters are estimated from a structural model and a reduced-form model. Firstly, this study departs from the existing literature in the sense that it does not assume or predict a linear effect of oil prices on state taxes. Instead, we find a nonlinear concave relationship between state taxes and oil prices, which implies that higher oil prices lead to diminishing marginal returns in state taxes. Secondly, our findings corroborate the notable hypothesis of Kilian's (2008) study, which states that oil price shocks are not all created equal. Here, we find a negative average response of state taxes to changes in oil prices for periods led by negative oil supply shocks (for example, the Arab Spring). Alternatively, we find the opposite effect, for periods led by positive oil demand shocks and positive oil supply shocks (for example, the oil price boom of the early 2000s and the 2014 oil glut). Lastly, we find strong distributional effects of oil price shocks on state taxes: oildependent states (Alaska, Oklahoma, Wyoming, Texas, New Mexico, North Dakota, and Louisiana) face a more elastic and volatile response of state taxes to changes in oil prices compared to other states. For tax policy implications, our model predicts that motor fuel consumption is overtaxed relative to its importance in the consumer price index.

title: tidyMacro: A Fast, Tidy Toolkit for Applied Macroeconometrics
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt

detail.title: tidyMacro: A Fast, Tidy Toolkit for Applied Macroeconometrics
detail.abstract: tidyMacro is an R package that provides a fast,unified toolkit for applied macroeconometric analysis. It supports reduced-form VAR estimation, together with a comprehensive set of structural identification schemes: recursive (short-run), long-run, external instruments (proxy-SVAR) for both invertible and non-invertible shocks, internal instruments and heteroskedasticity-based identification. Inference is delivered through several bootstrap routines: The package further provides forecast error variance decompositions, historical decompositions, and formal diagnostics for external-instrument validity. Four local projections (LP) estimators are exposed under a common formula grammar: classical LP-OLS, LP with instrumental variables (LP-IV), panel LP with time-clustered inference and optional small-sample refinement, and LP difference in differences. The computational engine is written in C++ via Rcpp and RcppArmadillo, with OpenMP parallelism across bootstrap replications and horizons, while the R layer follows tidyverse conventions and returns tidy tibbles and ggplot2 objects. Replication datasets ship with the package so that canonical empirical applications can be reproduced end-to-end.

title: Customer-Related Disclosures: Information Transmission and Financial Coordination Along the Supply Chain
affiliations: Bocconi, Tulane University - A.B. Freeman School of Business and University of Miami - Department of Accounting

detail.title: Customer-Related Disclosures: Information Transmission and Financial Coordination Along the Supply Chain
detail.abstract: We examine whether firms' voluntary discussion of their major customers during quarterly earnings conference calls conveys incremental, decision-relevant information about those customers and affects financial coordination along the supply chain. Using supplier-customer links from annual 10-K major-customer disclosures and a sentence-level FinBERT sentiment analysis of 44,102 supplier-customer quarters between 2002 and 2023, we isolate the incremental content of firms' customer-related commentary after accounting for abnormal pre-call business press coverage of the customer. Customers experience significantly negative abnormal returns when suppliers disclose bad news and explicitly name them, with no comparable reaction on good-news calls. These revised market expectations are borne out in realized subsequent performance: the volume and negative tone of firms' customer-related disclosures are associated with lower current and future customer earnings, while positive commentary is not, and customer-related commentary corresponds to greater subsequent business press coverage of those customers. Finally, more positive discussion corresponds to longer customer payment periods and more negative discussion to shorter ones, consistent with creditworthiness-based adjustments in trade credit and supply chain finance. Our results suggest that firms' voluntary disclosures about their customers are a meaningful channel of information transmission and financial coordination within supply-chain networks.

title: Above-Range IPO Pricing and Aftermarket Underperformance: Evidence and a Valuation Confound

detail.title: Above-Range IPO Pricing and Aftermarket Underperformance: Evidence and a Valuation Confound

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Do large, publicized initial public offerings (IPOs) follow a repeatable, tradeable post-listing price path? I study two samples: 38 prominent IPOs from 2019–2026, and every U.S. IPO raising at least $500 million from January 2024 through June 2026 (n = 60), selected mechanically, measuring each name's first 120 trading days against sector exchange-traded funds (ETFs), Fama–French factors, and calendar-time portfolios, with every test pre-registered. There is no common price shape: peak days span the full window, so the folk pattern fails as description. What does separate the sample is an order-book measure fixed before trading begins: IPOs priced above their filing range subsequently underperform, with median beta-adjusted alpha of −31% against −9% for other deals (Holm-adjusted p = 0.035; calendar-time spread t = −2.17), holding within each listing vintage and within sectors, while the first-day pop predicts nothing. That reading carries an important qualification. Above-range names also carry systematically richer valuation multiples (rank correlation +0.49), and a pre-registered valuation-tercile control cannot separate above-range pricing from the price-to-sales gradient in long-run IPO returns documented by Ritter (2026); the effect is therefore reported as a conditional regularity whose independence from valuation richness is not established here. The decline is gradual, concentrated between trading days 20 and 100 rather than around earnings events; its unconditional level, though not its cross-sectional ordering, depends on the risk model. The evidence is consistent with divergence-of-opinion overpricing under early short-sale constraints. One registered test failed with the opposite sign and is reported as such.

title: On the Divergence of Calvo and Rotemberg Pricing and the Sustainability of the Standard Paradox of Flexibility Solution at the Zero Lower Bound
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: On the Divergence of Calvo and Rotemberg Pricing and the Sustainability of the Standard Paradox of Flexibility Solution at the Zero Lower Bound
detail.abstract: The standard New Keynesian literature, notably the Werning (2011) framework, models Zero Lower Bound (ZLB) episodes as finite-duration negative natural interest rate shocks. This paper mathematically demonstrates that the non-linear solution under ZLB fundamentally diverges between Calvo and Rotemberg pricing environments due to the presence of price dispersion as a state variable in the former. The standard deflationary ZLB equilibrium cannot be maintained in the full nonlinear Calvo model regardless of an economy-wide or industry-wide labor market, and Eggertsson and Singh (2019) neglects an additional nonlinear constraint.

title: Reclassification and Reverse Migration in Corporate AI Investment: Propositions for a Dynamic Capital Allocation Model

detail.title: Reclassification and Reverse Migration in Corporate AI Investment: Propositions for a Dynamic Capital Allocation Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial or personal relationships with any person or organization that could be perceived to have influenced this work. The author is an independent researcher with no institutional affiliation and no commercial interest in any product, vendor, or firm discussed.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual paper. It involves no human participants, no animal subjects, and no primary or personal data collection.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no funding from any agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
Corporate investment in artificial intelligence has grown rapidly, yet firms remain largely unable to demonstrate where that capital generates economic value. This paper argues that a significant part of the difficulty is a classification problem rather than a measurement problem. Standard capital allocation practice assigns an investment to a category once, at the point of commitment, and holds that assignment fixed for the life of the asset. AI investments violate the assumption underlying that practice, because the source of uncertainty that governs their value changes as technical feasibility, market validation, and organizational capability resolve at different times and at different rates.

The paper develops a dynamic model of AI capital allocation organized around two dimensions, payoff predictability and commitment irreversibility, that jointly define three economic states: AI Research and Development, in which value derives from uncertainty reduction; AI Strategic Option, in which value derives from preserved flexibility; and AI Capital Expenditure, in which value derives from measurable operating returns. The model specifies the conditions under which an investment migrates between states and, in contrast with maturity-stage models, treats migration as bidirectional: re-emergent technical, competitive, regulatory, or organizational uncertainty can return a mature deployment to an earlier economic state, and the valuation logic applied to it should revert accordingly.

Seven propositions are advanced. Two are the paper's principal claims. First, migration from Strategic Option to Capital Expenditure requires the joint resolution of market uncertainty and organizational readiness; resolution of market uncertainty alone is insufficient, and treating it as sufficient is a systematic source of premature scaling. Second, reverse migration is a normal state of the system rather than a project failure, and firms lacking an explicit mechanism to recognize it will systematically overstate the reliability of forecast returns on mature AI assets. The paper operationalizes each construct into measurable indicators and specifies an empirical design through which the propositions can be tested. The contribution is theoretical and the propositions are untested; they are offered as falsifiable conjectures, not as findings.

title: Skill or Sustainability? Deconstructing The Stock-selection Timing Abilities of European ESG Fund Managers
affiliations: , National and Kapodistrian University of Athens - Faculty of Economics, School of Economics & Political Science and National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

detail.title: Skill or Sustainability? Deconstructing The Stock-selection Timing Abilities of European ESG Fund Managers
detail.abstract: Purpose-Driven by the rapid expansion of ESG investing and the heightened volatility recently observed in the financial landscape, we investigate the stock-selection timing abilities of ESG fund managers. Design/methodology/approach-We employ a novel holdings-based stock-selection timing test targeting funds operating within the leading European markets for sustainable investing-the UK, France, and Germanyspanning the period from January 1, 2012, to December 31, 2024. Findings-Bootstrap analysis reveals that 25.76% of UK funds exhibit timing abilities that cannot be attributed to luck, though positive timers remain fewer than among conventional peers. Conversely, French and German managers generally fail to time active trades successfully. Nonetheless, strategy efficacy is weakened during turbulent periods. Notably, positive timers generate significantly higher Fama-French-six-factor abnormal returns than negative timers at the short-term six-month horizon, with return spreads ranging from 2.72% to 4.68% across all regions. Timing skills correlate positively with active trading but negatively with ESG ratings. Finally, UK and German fund investors recognize adept timers, whereas French ones do not. Practical implications-Our results provide crucial insights for market participants, highlighting that France's strong ESG integration and government incentives may create an environment that disincentivizes active timing, leading investors to prioritize social impact over financial performance. Originality/value-To the best of our knowledge, this study represents the first empirical attempt to evaluate the stock-selection timing abilities of ESG fund managers within the European context.

title: Which World gets Covered? Media Ideology and the Geography of Foreign News
affiliations: and

detail.title: Which World gets Covered? Media Ideology and the Geography of Foreign News

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors report there are no competing interests to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Scholarship on foreign news coverage has long assumed that the geographic media coverage converges across outlets, driven by the characteristics of countries and events rather than the politics of the press. We challenge this assumption by arguing that media ideology shapes the symbolic boundaries of political community and, consequently, the geography of news. We expect culturally conservative outlets-which emphasize national identity and express greater skepticism toward globalization-to devote less attention to foreign places and concentrate their foreign coverage closer to home, compared to culturally progressive outlets. Meanwhile, economically rightist outlets are oriented toward markets and international integration, so they should exhibit the opposite pattern, compared to their economically leftist counterparts. We test these arguments using a novel dataset of one million news articles that are quasi-randomly selected from the Anglophone internet. This allows us to integrate ideological scores for 324 major media outlets across 26 countries around the world. We measure geographic coverage by geocoding 2.76 million place references via named entity recognition, automated gazetteer querying, and a custom algorithm. The results consistently support our expectations: cultural conservatism is associated with less foreign coverage and, when covering foreign places, more geographically proximate coverage, whereas economic rightism is associated with more foreign and distant coverage. These findings demonstrate that media ideology shapes both political interpretation and geographic news exposure, with significant implications for citizens' geopolitical knowledge, political attitudes, and behavior.

title: Shake it till you Strand it? Economic Assessment of Clay Shrinkage-swelling Risk in a Warming France
affiliations: , Paris Dauphine University, Square Research Center and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Shake it till you Strand it? Economic Assessment of Clay Shrinkage-swelling Risk in a Warming France

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This work benefitted from the research grant "Stranded Assets" awarded by La Banque Postale.

detail.abstract: This paper studies clay shrinkage-swelling (CSS), the subsidence of buildings on clay soils during droughts, one of the costliest and fastest-growing perils for French housing. We build a forward-looking pipeline that projects municipality-level CSS hazard through 2100 under climate scenarios, converts it into the present value of expected future damage, and tests whether these projected costs are reflected in transaction prices. Across a large sample of detached-house sales, CSS risk is only weakly capitalized: projected losses reach several percent of house value in the most exposed municipalities, yet the associated price discounts are close to zero. Using claim-level insurance data, we further show that repair costs have a heavy right tail, so that average-cost measures understate the exposure to stranding. We argue that this limited capitalization is not, in itself, evidence of market failure. Under the French natural-catastrophe regime, drought damage is largely socialized, which can make weak capitalization privately rational. As the ongoing reform of that regime shifts a growing share of the cost onto individual premiums and deductibles, the physical risk we quantify becomes a latent repricing risk that could capitalize abruptly.

title: Does the Tone of Earnings Press Releases Predict Stock Returns? Evidence From S&P 500 Firms, 2022-2024
affiliations: Del Norte High Jr Sr High School

detail.title: Does the Tone of Earnings Press Releases Predict Stock Returns? Evidence From S&P 500 Firms, 2022-2024

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All data sources used are free and publicly available: SEC EDGAR, Yahoo Finance, and open-source software.

detail.abstract: This paper tests whether the language a company uses to announce its earnings predicts its stock's reaction beyond whether it beat or missed expectations. I collected 6,013 earnings press releases from S&P 500 firms between 2022 and 2024 from SEC EDGAR, scored each using FinBERT, and computed market-model-adjusted abnormal returns around each announcement. Using OLS with two-way clustered standard errors, I find that more positive press release wording predicts higher abnormal returns across all three event windows, and that relationship holds after controlling for the earnings beat-or-miss. All six regressions are significant at p < 0.0001. A placebo test on random non-earnings dates produces near-zero coefficients, confirming the effect is specific to announcement windows. The correlation between sentiment and earnings surprise is only 0.029, directly ruling out the objection that tone is just a reflection of a good beat. How a company frames its results carries information the headline figure does not. All data and code are publicly available.

title: How the Financing of Balance-Sheet Policy Shapes Its Effects

detail.title: How the Financing of Balance-Sheet Policy Shapes Its Effects
detail.abstract: I ask whether Federal Reserve balance-sheet policy has the same effect on real GDP and the price level when different liabilities finance it. To answer, I develop HARS-Z by extending HARS, the sampler of Kim and Zha (2026), to include zero restrictions alongside shock heteroskedasticity, sign restrictions, and narrative restrictions. On monthly U.S. data I identify two balance-sheet shocks, one financed by reserves and one by overnight reverse repurchases (ON RRP). The estimated transmission differs across the two financing channels in the variable that responds. At the 90% level the reserve-financed contraction lowers GDP without a deflator decline, and the ON RRP-financed contraction lowers the GDP deflator without a GDP decline. Local projections on the identified shocks reach the first links of the money channel. The reserve-financed contraction lowers total bank deposits and raises the funds spread over interest on reserves. The ON RRP-financed contraction moves neither.

title: Observable Equilibrium Footprints under External Housing Purchasing-Capacity Shocks

detail.title: Observable Equilibrium Footprints under External Housing Purchasing-Capacity Shocks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study is based exclusively on publicly available aggregated data and did not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Empirical housing research observes the outcomes of market adjustment, but not the adjustment process itself. Existing studies have documented how housing markets respond through prices, residential sorting, transaction activity, and structural constraints, yet these dimensions are usually analysed separately. This paper develops an empirical framework for reconstructing housing-market adjustment by interpreting multiple observable outcomes as Observable Equilibrium Footprints: complementary empirical signatures of an otherwise unobservable equilibrium process. Using a municipality-year panel for the Balearic Islands from 2015 to 2023 and a shift-share measure of external housing purchasing-capacity shocks, the analysis examines resident composition, transaction dynamics, aggregate income indicators, and housing prices. The evidence reveals a consistent hierarchy. External purchasing-capacity shocks are most clearly reflected in resident composition and transaction activity, become weaker in aggregate income indicators, and are least pronounced in contemporaneous average housing prices. These findings suggest that housing-market adjustment under external pressure may first become visible through composition and participation before being compressed into aggregate price outcomes. The framework shifts attention from identifying a single best indicator of adjustment to interpreting multiple observable footprints jointly, offering a general empirical approach for reconstructing market processes that cannot be directly observed.

title: Why does Gendered Language Matter? Evidence on the Cultural and Cognitive Channels
affiliations: Union College - Department of Economics and Curtin University - Centre for Research in Applied Economics

detail.title: Why does Gendered Language Matter? Evidence on the Cultural and Cognitive Channels

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no competing interests. Mavisakalyan receives funding from the Australian Government through the Australian Research Council Centre of Excellence for the Elimination of Violence Against Women (project number CE230100004).

detail.abstract: Does speaking a gendered language affect an individual's support for gender roles, or does it simply indicate that an individual comes from a more patriarchal culture? We exploit differences in the gender structure of an individual's mother tongue and that of their interview language to empirically identify the cognitive and cultural effects of language influence. We find that the cognitive channel of influence on support for patriarchal values is three times the size of the cultural channel and roughly on par with the effect of gender itself. Future work should pay greater attention to the grammatical structure of interview languages.

title: A Collateral-Adjusted Hartwick Rule with Biodiversity Thresholds and Sovereign Debt

detail.title: A Collateral-Adjusted Hartwick Rule with Biodiversity Thresholds and Sovereign Debt

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, financial, professional, or other relationships with any individuals or organizations that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, the research reported in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it is a theoretical research article and did not involve human participants, patients, animals, personal data, or case-study subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: We develop a dynamic sovereign-wealth model for resource-rich economies in which exhaustible-resource rents, biodiversity conservation, public debt, and sovereign collateral are jointly determined. The government manages produced capital, renewable natural capital, biodiversity, an exhaustible mineral stock, official gold reserves, secured and unsecured debt, and outstanding collateral positions. Monetary gold and future mineral-fiscal receipts can lower the cost of a secured debt tranche, but pledging them reduces crisis liquidity, changes creditor priority, and may create pressure to accelerate extraction. The model makes three distinctions that are often blurred in policy discussions: underground mineral wealth is an exhaustible natural asset; biodiversity supports the productivity and regeneration of renewable natural capital; and monetary gold is a financial reserve asset whose ownership is distinct from its pledgeability. We separate the general discounted-welfare problem from the regular-maximin benchmark required for a Hartwick-type result. Along a regular constant-consumption path, zero shadow-valued genuine investment yields a collateraladjusted Hartwick condition: mineral depletion and additional encumbrance must be offset by accumulation of productive, ecological, or financial assets, or by debt reduction. Binding ecological thresholds create minimum restoration obligations that cannot be replaced by ordinary capital accumulation. A strictly concave collateral problem delivers a unique optimal collateral portfolio, possibly at a boundary, and defines a nature-consistent borrowing base using only mineral revenues obtainable along ecologically viable extraction paths. A resourcerevenue coverage covenant generates an explicit financing wedge in the extraction condition and can contribute to a debt-collateral-biodiversity trap. Finally, debt above the present value of viable primary surpluses cannot be made sustainable by changing claim priority alone. The framework provides a theoretical foundation for natural-capital-adjusted debt sustainability analysis, gold-backed sovereign finance, resource-backed lending rules, and debt-for-nature interventions.

title: Property Rights with Multiple Assets and Scarce Investment Capacity

detail.title: Property Rights with Multiple Assets and Scarce Investment Capacity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Property-rights theory suggests that residual rights of control should be assigned to the investing agent. We show that this logic can fail when one investor allocates scarce investment capacity across multiple assets. Asset ownership then affects not only investment incentives, but also how investment is allocated across assets. With abundant capacity, the standard incentive effect dominates, so assigning all assets to the investor is optimal. With scarce capacity, assigning all assets to the non-investor can instead be optimal, as it removes ownership-induced distortions in investment allocation. At intermediate capacity, mixed ownership can emerge by balancing the incentive and allocation effects.

title: “The Winner Takes It All”: On the Optimal Design of Multidimensional Tullock Contests With Category-Prizes and Aggregation Rules”
affiliations: Maastricht University

detail.title: “The Winner Takes It All”: On the Optimal Design of Multidimensional Tullock Contests With Category-Prizes and Aggregation Rules”

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The corresponding author has nothing to disclose regarding potential conflicts of interests.
declarations.funderStatement: The corresponding author has nothing to disclose regarding funding.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the optimal prize structure for a two-dimensional Tullock contest with two participants, where the probability of winning the multidimensional prize is separable from winning the two one-dimensional prizes. In this unique setting, where the strict quasiconcave effort aggregation rule of the contest designer is known to the players with strict quasiconvex multidimensional cost functions, a unique Pure-strategy Nash-Equilibrium exists. The results show that under these conditions and mild assumptions on the one-dimensional ability levels of the contestants for example a wide range of prize structures are optimal. Nevertheless, when introducing risk aversion in the model or when introducing contestant dependent weights for the effort aggregation rule, the number of optimal prize structures declines. The latter, does not hold when introducing contestant dependent weights in the case that both the effort aggregation rule and multidimensional cost functions are linear.

title: Auditing and Improving the Alignment Between Deep Model Attention and Pharmacopoeia Diagnostic Regions for Explainable Herbal Medicine Identification
affiliations: Kyung Hee University, Kyung Hee University, Kyung Hee University, Kyung Hee University, Kyung Hee University, Kyung Hee University and Kyung Hee University

detail.title: Auditing and Improving the Alignment Between Deep Model Attention and Pharmacopoeia Diagnostic Regions for Explainable Herbal Medicine Identification
detail.abstract: Accurate identification of herbal medicines is essential for drug safety, yet organoleptic evaluation of cross-sections is subjective and limited by the declining number of experts. The engineering application addressed in this work is automated and auditable herbal medicine identification. Its artificial intelligence (AI) contribution is a framework that quantifies and improves the agreement between deep model attention and pharmacopoeia-defined diagnostic regions. These diagnostic regions are the anatomical structures designated by pharmacopoeia guidelines, such as the cambium, medullary rays, and pith. We convert these criteria into per-species radial location priors through automatic cambium detection and sigma-based boundary definition, and we measure the overlap between model activation maps and these priors using the Intersection over Union (IoU). Across four Polygonaceae species, five deep networks classified accurately (F1 score 0.88 to 0.97) on background-removed images, yet their attention showed low overlap with the pharmacopoeia priors (IoU 0.18 to 0.30) on held-out data. We then introduce an architecture-aware attention supervision loss that extracts the native attention of convolutional neural network and Transformer models and guides it toward the priors. Supervision raised the overlap in four of five models (for example ConvNeXt-B from 0.267 to 0.374 and DenseNet-121 from 0.245 to 0.355, false discovery rate corrected p < 0.001) while maintaining classification accuracy. The framework provides a reproducible and quantitative basis for auditing and improving the agreement between model attention and pharmacopoeia criteria in explainable herbal medicine identification.

title: Regulatory Burden or Market Reconfiguration? What Post-Dodd-Frank Swap Data Shows

detail.title: Regulatory Burden or Market Reconfiguration? What Post-Dodd-Frank Swap Data Shows
detail.abstract:
The G-20 nations committed to swap market reforms following the financial crisis of 2007-08. In the U.S., these reforms were enacted under the Dodd-Frank Act. The interventions were deep and comprehensive, and many commentators raised concerns with their costs. A natural question is whether the reforms deter parties from using swaps, which among other things are a socially useful tool for risk management. The downfall of Silicon Valley Bank due to its failure to manage interest rate risk only makes this question more timely. This Article uses Federal Reserve data from 2000 to 2025 to study the use of derivatives by banking firms.

Depending on the perspective, evidence can be found to support either that regulation depressed swap usage or that regulation did not interfere with the use of swaps to manage risk. Looking across asset classes, those that were most affected by regulation (interest rate and credit default swaps) experience substantial declines while those exempt from some regulation (foreign exchange and equity swaps) experience substantial growth. Looking at the use of swaps relative to other instruments (futures, options and forwards), before and after the onset of swap regulation, however, shows that hedging with swaps became relatively more popular after the onset of regulation. Delving deeper into the cross-instrument perspective, comparing smaller institutions that were exempt from some of the most onerous obligations to larger, non-exempt institutions, the evidence is ambiguous as to whether the treated group (i.e., non-exempt institutions) reduced using swaps relative to other instruments in the post-regulatory period. The paper shows how statistics can be used rhetorically to further or oppose the regulatory project, and that a conclusive assessment of how Dodd-Frank regulation impacted swap usage is elusive.

title: The Gambler Was Right: A Reproducible Challenge to Strategic Indifference in Fair Coin Sequences
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Gambler Was Right: A Reproducible Challenge to Strategic Indifference in Fair Coin Sequences

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study involved no human or animal participants; all data are computationally generated.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant funding from any funding agency, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: In a memoryless process, each event is independent of every prior event; it seems to follow, as a logical entailment, that the timing of an observer's engagement cannot affect outcome distributions. We term this conclusion strategic indifference and test it directly in computationally generated fair coin flip sequences. It fails. Two players observe the same sequences of 80 binary outcomes across 500,000 sequences (40 million flips), make the same number of 9-bet anti-continuation wagers, and face identical per-entry loss odds of (1/2)^9. They differ only in entry criterion: the selective player enters after observing T consecutive same-side outcomes (T ∈ {3, 4, 5, 6, 7}); the Markov player enters at each direction change. Under equalized comparison, the selective player experiences 10.6% to 67.7% fewer catastrophic losses, scaling monotonically with observation depth, with zero gradient reversals across 25 data points and combined Z-scores from-7.16 to-22.60-decisive after conservative correction for within-sequence correlation. Yet per-entry loss rates confirm independence: both players match (1/2)^9 at every threshold. The effect is positional, not predictive. The mechanism is path narrowing: prior observations consume positions within the streak structure, raising the effective catastrophe threshold without altering any individual flip probability. The advantage scales inversely with sequence length, converging with Miller and Sanjurjo's (2018) finite-sequence streak bias and demonstrating that their retrospective finding operates prospectively. The result decomposes the Gambler's Fallacy into a per-event prediction (false) and a strategic entry prescription (true); full code is provided for independent reproduction.

title: From Demographic Dividend to Demographic Maturity: Forecasting Population Ageing & Economic Growth in Kerala & Uttar Pradesh
affiliations: and University of Calcutta

detail.title: From Demographic Dividend to Demographic Maturity: Forecasting Population Ageing & Economic Growth in Kerala & Uttar Pradesh
detail.abstract: This study investigates the divergent demographic and economic trajectories of Kerala and Uttar Pradeshtwo Indian states at opposite ends of the demographic spectrum. Using demographic and economic data (1991-2023) and recent official reports and peer-reviewed studies, we conduct a comparative analysis to answer: (1) How do Kerala and UP differ in population ageing and fertility patterns? (2) What are the projected trends in their old-age dependency ratios (OADR) and elderly population shares (EPS)? (3) How might these differences affect labor markets and economic growth? Guided by the Demographic Transition Model and the theory of the demographic dividend (Bloom & Canning, 2003), we formulate hypotheses that Kerala's low fertility and high longevity have produced a rapidly ageing population with high dependency burdens, whereas Uttar Pradesh's higher fertility has preserved a younger age structure. We analyze time-series data and incorporate official population projections (TGPP, 2020) and survey findings (LASI 2021). The results confirm stark contrasts: Kerala's total fertility rate (~1.5) is well below UP's (~2.4), and its elderly share (~16.5% in 2023) and OADR (~0.26) are roughly double those of Uttar Pradesh (elderly ~8.6%; OADR ~0.13). Official projections suggest Kerala's elderly share will rise to ~23% by 2036, while UP's will reach ~12%. Labor force participation trends also diverge: Kerala's working-age labor force has stagnated (female LFPR very low), whereas UP has seen rapid growth (including a jump in female participation from 14% to 36% from 2018 to 2024). In the Results/Analysis, we detail these findings using tables and a comparative chart. The Discussion interprets the economic implications: Kerala's ageing portends increased fiscal and social support needs (pensions, healthcare) and a shrinking workforce, while UP's youthfulness represents a potential demographic dividend if accompanied by investment in human capital and female employment. Policy implications include Kerala strengthening elderly social programs and possibly raising retirement age, and UP continuing reforms (such as women's workforce access) to harness its young labor force. In Conclusion, we argue that the demographic divide between Kerala and Uttar Pradesh necessitates tailored economic strategies. This study contributes a rigorous analysis of state-level ageing and labor trends, with wider relevance for regions with similar contrasts.

title: A Quantitative Analysis of Macro-fashion Indicators: Testing the Hemline, Lipstick, and Corporate Wear Indexes
affiliations: University of New South Wales (UNSW)

detail.title: A Quantitative Analysis of Macro-fashion Indicators: Testing the Hemline, Lipstick, and Corporate Wear Indexes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or primary data collection requiring ethics approval. All data used are publicly available secondary sources (IMF GDP data, published academic studies, Google Trends, and independently coded imagery
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Fashion and economics are usually treated as separate worlds, but this paper tests whether that separation holds up empirically. I look at three commonly cited signals-the lipstick effect, the hemline index, and the recent rise of corporate dressing-as possible indicators of the business cycle. Using a 30-country cross-section for the Hemline Index and a seven-year US time series for the Lipstick Index, I find strong support for the Hemline Index (R² = 0.674, p < 0.001), but no significant relationship for the Lipstick Index once the full sample is used (R² = 0.032, p = 0.70). The Corporate Wear section relies on Google Trends data descriptively rather than as a formally estimated model, since no suitable incidence data was available. The main takeaway isn't about any single indicator so much as the difference between them: some macro-fashion signals hold up to scrutiny, and some don't and working out which is which is more useful than assuming all three are equally credible.

title: EPC Mirage: Grid Decarbonisation can Overstate Retrofit Progress in Carbon-weighted Building Energy Ratings
affiliations: Imperial College London and University of Navarra, IESE Business School

detail.title: EPC Mirage: Grid Decarbonisation can Overstate Retrofit Progress in Carbon-weighted Building Energy Ratings

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it relied exclusively on publicly available administrative data and involved no human-participant recruitment or intervention.

detail.abstract: Energy labels shape decarbonisation policy and investment, yet carbon-weighted ratings can improve when electricity systems change but buildings do not. We exploit the June 2022 revision to the methodology for non-domestic Energy Performance Certificates (EPCs) in England and Wales as a register-scale accounting discontinuity. Of 106,228 premises with repeat EPC assessments spanning the revision, 80.5% received better ratings, with gains concentrated among electricity-exposed premises and no comparable break in aggregate, unlinked metered-energy indicators. A cross-fitted, doubly robust estimator yields 94,911 expected EPC-B reclassifications across 57.2 million m 2 , a notional retrofit-expenditure equivalent of £5.7 billion. France's 2026 electricity primary-energy coefficient revision similarly moves 103,085 certificates out of F/G, 89.1% among electrically heated certificates. Policy should separate carbon accounting from physical-performance standards, enabling a least-cost mix of cleaner energy supply and targeted retrofit rather than counting grid decarbonisation as building improvement.

title: Canadian Financial Infrastructure Exploited in Transnational Fraud

detail.title: Canadian Financial Infrastructure Exploited in Transnational Fraud
detail.abstract:
This report examines the convergence of generative artificial intelligence, cryptocurrency laundering infrastructure, and cross-border social engineering in the evolution of romance scam-enabled financial crime affecting Canadian institutions. Drawing on reporting from the Federal Bureau of Investigation Internet Crime Complaint Center (FBI IC3), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP), and blockchain analytics firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs, the analysis identifies a measurable transition from opportunistic, manually-operated fraud schemes toward industrialized transnational operations. 

The report documents how AI-generated personas, deepfake impersonation tools, and multilingual automation systems have reduced operational costs for fraud actors while increasing victim acquisition at scale. Particular attention is given to cryptocurrency laundering pathways — including stablecoin conversion, decentralized finance (DeFi) layering, cross-chain transfers, and over-the-counter (OTC) broker off-ramping — that exploit the opacity of digital asset ecosystems and exceed the detection capabilities of traditional threshold-based anti-money laundering (AML) monitoring systems. The report further assesses Canada's specific vulnerability profile, attributing heightened exposure to widespread Interac e-Transfer adoption, high public trust in digital financial systems, and fragmented cross-border compliance coordination. 

Three systemic risk vectors are identified and analyzed: the industrialization of victim acquisition, increased laundering opacity through decentralized cryptocurrency infrastructure, and the systematic exploitation of Canadian digital payment rails. Recommendations are directed at the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Nigerian financial intelligence agencies, and Canadian financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms.

title: Turbulence in Agricultural Markets: Climate Regime Asymmetry, Rough Volatility Structure, and Regime-Switching Ensemble Forecasting

detail.title: Turbulence in Agricultural Markets: Climate Regime Asymmetry, Rough Volatility Structure, and Regime-Switching Ensemble Forecasting
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between Pacific climate variability and agricultural commodity market volatility across three methodological layers. First, using 24 years of daily wheat futures data, we document a statistically significant asymmetry in the effect of El Nino-Southern Oscillation on realised volatility: La Nina conditions raise annualised wheat volatility 15.2 percent above neutral periods (t = 12.91, p < 0.001), while El Nino shows no significant effect (t = 0.21, p = 0.833). This finding is robust to exclusion of the 2022 Ukraine war period (8.3 percent premium, t = 7.8, p < 0.001). Second, we estimate the Hurst exponent of wheat log-volatility using structure functions across moment orders q = 0.5 to 2.0, finding H = 0.134. This is substantially below the Brownian motion benchmark of H = 0.5 and below the equity market estimate of H = 0.197 reported by Gatheral, Jaisson, and Rosenbaum (2018), consistent with Kolmogorov's turbulence cascade mathematics applied to agricultural commodity markets. Third, we train a Transformer-based classifier on a panel of 11 agricultural commodity markets and combine it with GARCH through a climate regime-switching rule. The resulting ensemble significantly outperforms GARCH during normal climate periods (AUC 0.669 versus 0.636, p = 0.036, one-sided bootstrap), while GARCH dominates during La Nina through volatility persistence. The finding that no single model captures both regimes simultaneously has direct implications for food security early warning systems.

title: The Factor Zoo Audit: Testing the Durability of Published Stock Market Premiums

detail.title: The Factor Zoo Audit: Testing the Durability of Published Stock Market Premiums

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently and is not funded by any organization. The author has no financial or personal relationships with any entity that could influence this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research uses publicly available archival financial data from the Ken French Data Library and does not involve human subjects. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agency. The research was conducted independently.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we investigate whether the five classical stock return factors (i.e., market, size, value, profitability, and momentum) still have the announced alphas after 2010 and remain statistically significant when trading costs are considered realistically. Using pre-registered hypotheses, Harvey-Liu-Zhu significance framework (t ≥ 3.0), and explicit transaction cost assumptions, we find: (1) out of six factors, five have decayed after 2010 and both value and size premiums have even changed their signs; (2) when the cost level is set at 15 basis points, none of the factors but the market premium can be regarded as statistically significant; (3) the market premium has survived and strengthened, which suggests persistent fundamentals in risk versus statistical illusion in anomaly premiums.

title: Speculation in Commodity Futures and Domestic Food Price Transmission Evidence from 70 Food-Importing Countries, 2010-2021.
affiliations: Ege University and Bonn University

detail.title: Speculation in Commodity Futures and Domestic Food Price Transmission Evidence from 70 Food-Importing Countries, 2010-2021.
detail.abstract: This study examines whether speculative activity in agricultural commodity futures markets is associated with domestic food price transmission in food-importing economies. The analysis addresses the lack of multi-country evidence linking futures market positioning to retail price outcomes. Using a panel of 159,556 market-month observations across 70 countries and 2,811 markets over 2010-2021, the study combines data from the World Food Programme, Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Chicago Board of Trade, and IMF. The outcome variable is the domestic-to-futures price transmission ratio, defined as the log of domestic retail prices relative to futures prices in local currency. The key explanatory variable is managed money net long positioning as a share of open interest. The empirical strategy applies a two-way fixed effects model with market and time effects, complemented by an instrumental variables approach exploiting regulatory variation from the Dodd-Frank Act. The results show a negative and statistically significant association between speculative positioning and the transmission ratio in baseline estimates, indicating that increases in net long positions are associated with a widening gap between futures and domestic prices. However, instrumental variable estimates are imprecise and statistically insignificant, suggesting that the observed relationship is not robust to quasi-experimental identification. Robustness checks confirm sensitivity to specification and functional form. The findings provide crosscountry associational evidence on the link between futures market activity and domestic price transmission, but do not establish a definitive causal effect.

title: Regulation-Induced Greenwashing
affiliations: Northern Trust Corporation - Northern Trust Asset Management, CITIC Securities Co., Ltd and Griffith University - Griffith Business School

detail.title: Regulation-Induced Greenwashing
detail.abstract: Environmental policies are intended to strengthen resilience, but they may also create incentives for firms to appear greener without actually becoming greener. Exploiting the staggered finalization of U.S. State Climate Adaptation Plans in a stacked difference-indifferences design, we find that exposed firms increase greenwashing, as measured by both disclosure-performance gaps and greening talk in conference calls. The effect is strongest when external monitoring is weak, financial constraints are tight, climate exposure is high, and board oversight is limited. It is also more pronounced in climate-sensitive industries and in states with greater corruption or policy uncertainty. Greenwashing following plan finalization improves subsequent environmental ratings but is not accompanied by greater green patenting and is associated with weaker emissions outcomes, revealing a disconnect between perceived and substantive environmental performance. Despite this disconnect, firms engaging in greater post-policy greenwashing attract more institutional and ESG-oriented ownership, particularly through narrative-based green claims. These firms subsequently face higher costs of equity and overall capital, with weaker evidence for debt financing costs. The findings show how climate policy can unintentionally reward symbolic environmental responses while shifting their longer-run credibility costs to capital markets.

title: Downsian Competition for the Myerson Value
affiliations: Hitotsubashi University - Graduate School of Economics

detail.title: Downsian Competition for the Myerson Value
detail.abstract: This paper studies an electoral competition model in which parties maximize legislative power rather than vote shares. Voters are uniformly distributed on the unit interval and vote for the party proposing the closest policy platform. After the election, parties form coalitions through a communication network arising from ideological proximity: two parties are directly linked if their policy distance is at most d. A party's objective is its Myerson value in the resulting graph-restricted voting game. I characterize symmetric pure-strategy equilibria in two-, three-, and four-party systems. The two-party case yields convergence to the median. The three-party case admits a continuum of symmetric equilibria in which the two extreme parties are directly linked. In the four-party case, the unique symmetric equilibrium places two parties at (1-d)/2 and two parties at (1+d)/2. In both three-and four-party systems, more restrictive coalition communication, represented by a smaller d, generates a centripetal force, and the median voter theorem holds in the limit despite the multiparty setting.

title: From Displacement to Settlement A Scenario Framework for the AI Labor Transition, the Indian Transmission Channel, and a Firm Level Survival Audit

detail.title: From Displacement to Settlement A Scenario Framework for the AI Labor Transition, the Indian Transmission Channel, and a Firm Level Survival Audit
detail.abstract: This paper develops an end to end framework for the labor market transition induced by advanced artificial intelligence, extending the analysis past the moment of displacement to the economic equilibrium that follows it. A decomposition of the global labor force shows that even superhuman AI capability in cognitive domains directly exposes only about one fifth of world employment, and three displacement scenarios are constructed with assessed probabilities over a six to eight year window. The framework's central empirical case is India, whose export of cognitive labor creates a distinctive transmission channel: displacement occurring domestically even when AI adoption occurs abroad, propagating through the technology export engine, urban consumption, fiscal capacity, and demographic pressure. Evidence from 2026, including silent layoffs, collapsed entry level hiring, and the divergence between industry revenue growth of 6.1 percent and headcount growth of 2.3 percent, is shown to match the framework's predicted early signature, in which displacement manifests as underemployment and wage compression rather than headline unemployment. The paper then characterizes the transition as a rotation of economic activity toward five durable scarcities, models the post transition settlement, and contributes a firm level diagnostic, the Displacement Survival Audit, that converts the macro scenario into a scored, stress testable assessment of any operating business. The framework connects to the redistribution literature by identifying broad based asset ownership infrastructure as the settlement era's defining institution.

title: The Concept of Lawful Access and its Implications for User Freedoms in the EU Copyright Acquis: Opinion of the European Copyright Society
affiliations: Centre for IT & IP Law (CiTiP), Faculty of Law - KU Leuven, University of Glasgow - School of Law, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Juristische Fakultät, University of Amsterdam - Institute for Information Law (IViR) and University of Cyprus

detail.title: The Concept of Lawful Access and its Implications for User Freedoms in the EU Copyright Acquis: Opinion of the European Copyright Society

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The European Copyright Society (ECS) was founded in 2012 with the aim of creating a platform for critical and independent scholarly thinking on European Copyright Law and policy. Its members are scholars and academics from various countries of Europe, seeking to articulate and promote their views of the overall public interest on all topics in the field of authors rights, neighbouring rights and related matters. The ECS is neither funded nor instructed by any particular stakeholders. Its Opinions represent the independent views of a majority of ECS members.

detail.abstract: The advent of digital technologies and connected patterns of production and consumption has progressively displaced ownership in favour of access as the predominant mode of enjoyment of works of authorship and other information goods. This transition from acquiring physical copies to subscribing to digital services has become prevalent across various sectors and has even enabled new commercial, cultural and scientific practices. However, it also marks a major shift in the theory and function of copyright: it transforms a right primarily concerned with regulating certain exploitations and circulations of works into one capable of controlling individual acts of access and use. EU copyright law increasingly reflects this shift through conditions of lawfulness. These appear across the acquis in different forms: the “lawful acquirer” in the Software Directive, the “lawful user” in the Database Directive, “lawful use” and “lawful source” in the Information Society Directive and CJEU case law, and “lawful access” in the Text and Data Mining (TDM) provisions of the Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive (CDSMD). These expressions are not merely terminological variants. They perform a boundary-setting function by determining when exceptions and limitations may be relied upon, and therefore when certain acts may take place without right holders’ authorization. The principal risk, surfaced in decisions such as ACI Adam or VOB, is that lawful access, lawful use or lawful source might be equated with right holders’ authorization. An interpretation of this kind would undermine the nature and function of exceptions and limitations. Since an exception presupposes that authorization is not required, making authorization the sole condition of lawfulness would create circularity and deprive exceptions of practical effect. At the same time, lawfulness cannot be understood as an unlimited permission to access or use protected works. It must operate within identifiable legal boundaries, including effective technological protection measures, valid and enforceable contractual restrictions where not overridden by mandatory law, and other legally binding limits. Its application must also be guided by contextual principles, including the meaning of content “freely available online”, the knowledge and role of the user, the purpose and commercial or non-commercial character of the activity, the applicable fundamental rights framework, and the three-step test.

title: Youth-Type Blackhole Economy: Behavioral Rerouting and Future Effective Stock in Japan

detail.title: Youth-Type Blackhole Economy: Behavioral Rerouting and Future Effective Stock in Japan
detail.abstract:
This paper develops the Youth-Type Blackhole Economy as a theory of temporal disconnection in which present resources exist but fail to reinforce an efficient, credible, and recursively shared path to future livelihood security. The concept is not a synonym for poverty, low saving, or physical resource disappearance. Younger generations generate labor income, pay compulsory social insurance contributions, accumulate employment and contribution histories, and form human capital. The analytical problem arises when these resources are routed through channels whose conversion performance, portability, risk-sharing capacity, or perceived credibility is weak, causing resources to leave or fail to strengthen the shared risk-pooling circuit.

 The paper introduces a channel-based dynamic model. Objective Stock formation occurs through public, occupational, and private transfer routes, each with its own allocation share, conversion efficiency, and rate of return. Transtemporal trust is represented operationally by route-specific perceived credibility γ. It does not directly reduce objective Stock. It influences route choice, voluntary allocation, and reliance on liquid self-insurance. A decline in perceived credibility may therefore increase private saving for some individuals, increase liquidity preference for others, or increase current consumption for others. The common mechanism is not a uniform fall in total Stock, but the weakening or abandonment of a shared public temporal bridge and the resulting loss of risk pooling, continuity, and allocative efficiency. 

The model also includes a later-life release circuit in which accumulated Stock must be converted into current livelihood Flow. Objective barriers and subjective defensive preferences are separated. Public social insurance is treated as imperfectly substitutable with private accumulation because longevity pooling, disability and survivor protection, and broadly accessible inflation-adjusted lifetime claims cannot generally be replicated on equivalent terms through individual saving alone. This produces a temporal symmetry between forward disconnection in youth and release disconnection in later life.

A Cabinet Office survey item on old-age planning is presented only as an illustrative behavioral proxy. The paper explicitly identifies the age-period-cohort problem and does not infer cohort specific trust from one cross-section. The contribution is a falsifiable research framework for studying when institutionally transferred resources remain formally present yet generate welfare losses because participants reroute, duplicate, or immobilize resources in response to a channel they do not regard as credible.

title: A Dynamic Search and Matching Model of Foster Care: Theory and Evidence
affiliations: Nazarbayev University - Economics Department and Banco de México

detail.title: A Dynamic Search and Matching Model of Foster Care: Theory and Evidence
detail.abstract: This paper examines the two-sided dynamic matching problem in the US foster care system, where foster parents and children form reversible matches that may separate, persist, or transition to adoption. We first present new empirical facts on match transitions using administrative data. We then develop a two-sided search and matching model to rationalize these facts and generate predictions. Our findings show that a financial penalty on adoption exacerbates the intrinsic disadvantage faced by children with greater care needs and discourages high-quality matches from transitioning to adoption, highlighting important policy implications for improving permanency outcomes in foster care.

title: Forward and Reverse Bayesianism under Ambiguity

detail.title: Forward and Reverse Bayesianism under Ambiguity
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a model of ambiguity in which a decision maker may encounter new information and unforeseen contingencies simultaneously during a decision-making process. Focusing on constant independence preferences, the paper characterizes three methods of forward and reverse updating: the full Bayesian update and the maximum and minimum likelihood methods, all of which are consistent with Bayesianism. In all methods, Bayesianism requires that the prior and posterior belief sets satisfy a weaker form of rectangularity (Epstein and Schneider, 2003). This condition implies that the decision maker's probability perception over the current states may be independent of unobserved events and newly recognized events.

title: Economic-Aware Agentic Private Networks
affiliations: and Celona Inc.

detail.title: Economic-Aware Agentic Private Networks
detail.abstract: Private wireless networks are becoming the operating fabric of modern enterprises. In factories, ports, airports, warehouses, hospitals, mines, and energy sites, network decisions increasingly shape production continuity, worker safety, inspection quality, logistics flow, compliance, energy use, and operating cost. This paper introduces Economic-Aware Agentic Private Networks (Economic-Aware Agentic Private Networks), a framework for private wireless systems that bring enterprise value into the control loop. An Economic-Aware Agentic Private Network reasons over technical state, spectrum state, application criticality, business-economic state, historical evidence, and governance rules to select, validate, explain, and audit network actions. The framework combines business-intent translation, economic policy, retrieval and memory, supervisor and specialist agents, enterprise-utility scoring, digital-twin validation, governed actuation, and post-action verification. We formulate economic-aware control as constrained enterprise-utility maximization under cost, risk, energy, service-level, spectrum, safety, and approval constraints. We then develop a reference architecture, data model, closed-loop workflow, enterprise use cases, evaluation framework, and research roadmap. The central message is that private networks should evolve from KPI-driven automation toward business-aware control systems that act only when a network action creates enterprise value, respects operational risk, and satisfies governance.

title: Digital Payments and Retail Productivity: An Exploration with A Panel of U.S. Retail Subsectors
affiliations: Charles River Associates (CRA), Charles River Associates (CRA), Charles River Associates (CRA), Charles River Associates (CRA) and Charles River Associates (CRA)

detail.title: Digital Payments and Retail Productivity: An Exploration with A Panel of U.S. Retail Subsectors
