detail.abstract:
Background: In July 2025, WHO launched the “3 by 35” Initiative calling on countries to increase real prices of tobacco, alcohol, and sugary drinks by at least 50% by 2035 to secure an additional $ 1 trillion in public revenue. While the effectiveness of excise taxes and prices in reducing tobacco use is well-documented, the feasibility of this call to action has not been evaluated empirically across the world.​

Methods: Trend changes in countries’ nominal and inflation-adjusted retail prices were investigated using the most-sold brand of cigarettes over windows ranging from 2 to 16 years over the period 2008-2024, derived from nine editions of the  World Health Organization Report on the Global Tobacco Epidemic. Statistical models of the association of cigarette excise taxes and prices from the panel of 195 countries were estimated. The frequencies of cigarette prices rising by at least 20% and 50% over preceding periods was estimated, and the length of time countries would need to reach these target based on past trends were predicted. 

Findings: Over one- fifth of nominal cigarettes prices (and up to 40% in WHO’s African region) were sticky across successive periods, even in countries with high overall consumer price inflation. Between 2008 and 2024, inflation-adjusted international dollar cigarette prices rose at a least squares annual trend growth rate of 2·9% (95% UI 2·8–3·0%) Excise tax increases strongly predict price increases, with estimates from two-way fixed effects linear regression models suggesting taxes are  over-shifted to cigarette prices across country income groups, especially when specific excise taxes are introduced or increased. While large real price increases of over 50% were rare over a two-year window, one-third of countries saw real prices at least 50% higher than 10 years prior. We calculated country-specific growth rates of real price increases and the earliest year by which prices are predicted to rise by 20% and 50%.

Interpretation: Many of the instances of real price increases of 50% or more over 10-year periods occurred without countries implementing a conscious strategy to raise taxes. This, combined with the finding of a strong link between excise taxes and prices, suggests that it is feasible to achieve, and even surpass WHO’s 3 by 35 call to action for tobacco if countries strategize and accelerate tobacco tax increases.

title: The Associations of Environmental and Socioeconomic Risk Factors with Parkinson's Disease Incidence and Mortality across China

detail.title: The Associations of Environmental and Socioeconomic Risk Factors with Parkinson's Disease Incidence and Mortality across China

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no competing interests
declarations.funderStatement: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82404597, 82071552, 22376006, U23A20167).

detail.abstract:
Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) burden exhibits substantial regional disparities across China, yet the nonlinear synergistic impacts of air pollution, agrochemical exposure and socioeconomic factors on national PD incidence and mortality remain insufficiently characterized. 

Methods: Using 1990-2023 provincial panel data, this study applied Pearson correlation, Geodetector q-statistic, year-adjusted GAM and XGBoost-SHAP to examine linear, nonlinear and synergistic associations between five environmental-socioeconomic factors and PD burden. 

Findings: All five factors exerted distinct nonlinear effects on PD incidence and mortality, with incidence more susceptible to low-level pollution and early industrialization. PM₂.₅ and per capita industrial GDP showed unimodal risks, with thresholds of 50 μg/m³, 20,000 CNY (risk transition) and 40,000 CNY (risk saturation). Pesticide intensity followed a U-shaped association with minimal risk at 1,800 kg/km². Soil PAHs triggered staged toxicity rising sharply above 0.75 mg/kg, while soil DDT produced progressively increasing, plateauing risks beyond 0.2 mg/kg. Industrial expansion and agrochemical pollution exerted strong synergies elevating population PD burden. Machine learning generally validated GAM-derived nonlinear trends with minor threshold discrepancies. 

Interpretation: Atmospheric pollutants, soil persistent organic contaminants and socioeconomic factors synergistically and nonlinearly increase PD burden, and compound pollution amplifies adverse health risks. PD incidence is more susceptible to environmental exposures than long-term mortality. Thus, regional PD prevention requires integrated management of industrial growth, agrochemical use and soil pollution control. Stratified interventions based on validated risk thresholds facilitate targeted regional PD prevention.

detail.abstract:
Background: Emerging evidence from African and other low-and-middle -income populations suggests that a substantial proportion of apparent type 2 diabetes (T2D) cases occur at lower body mass index (BMI) (< 25kg/m2) and younger ages (<40 years) than seen in high-income populations. Whether this represents predominance of a distinct aetiology or reflects underlying population structure differences is unknown. We determined whether there is a disproportionate burden of T2D in non-overweight and/or younger individuals in an African population compared with a high-income population.

Methods: We analysed data from 24,985 adults aged ≥18 years from a Malawian population-based cross-sectional study (MEIRU) conducted between 2013 and 2016, and 41,937 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) conducted between 2009 and 2023.  We defined T2D as a fasting blood glucose level of ≥ 7mmol/L and/or a previously reported diagnosis.  We computed the crude and age-standardised prevalences across BMI groups and used logistic regression to compute adjusted odds ratios (95% CI) for the associations between participant characteristics and diabetes.

Results: A higher proportion of T2D cases in Malawi occurred in non-overweight individuals (34% [95% CI: 30,38%]) compared with Black (12% [8·7,18%]) and non-Black Americans (11% [9·3,13%]), which mirrored the underlying population distribution (Malawi non-overweight 69% [68·2,69·4%]) vs Black 23% [21·6,25·1%]) and non-Black Americans 30% [28·5,31·4%]). A greater proportion of T2D cases in Malawi occurred in individuals aged <40 years (24% [21,28%]) compared with Black (12% [8·2,17%]) and non-Black Americans (8% [6·8,9·6%]), also reflecting population structure, (Malawi aged <40y: 69%  [69·1,70·2%]), compared to Black Americans 42% [39·9,44·5%]) and non-Black Americans 37% [35·6-38·5%]).Age-standardised prevalence of T2D was lower among non-overweight Malawians than in the US population. For BMI <18·5 kg/m², a suggested cut-off for malnutrition-related diabetes, prevalence in Malawians was 1·3% (95% CI: 0·7, 2.0%) compared to  4·1% (2·2, 7·7%) in Black and 3·7% (1·8,7·6%) in non-Black Americans. Similarly, for BMI 18·5- 24·9 kg/m2, Malawian prevalence (2%) remained lower than that of Black and non-Black Americans (9·2% and 4·1%, respectively).Higher BMI and older age were strongly associated with T2D across all populations. Each 1 SD increase in BMI was associated with increased odds of T2D (OR 95% CI: 1·9, [1·8-2·0], 1·6, [1·4-1·8], and 1·9, [1·8-2·0]) as was each 1SD increase in age (2·1,[1·9-2·3]; 2·8, [2·4-3·3] and 2·9,[2·7-3·1])  in Malawian, Black Americans and non-Black Americans respectively.

Conclusion: The higher proportion of T2D cases occurring in leaner and younger individuals in African compared to high-income populations reflects differences in population BMI and age distribution rather than increased individual susceptibility at lower BMIs or younger ages.

title: Temperature Anomalies, Information Uncertainty, and Analysts' Earnings Forecasts
affiliations: National Sun Yat-Sen University and National Sun Yat-sen University

detail.title: Temperature Anomalies, Information Uncertainty, and Analysts' Earnings Forecasts
detail.abstract: As climate-related temperatures extremes have become increasingly frequent, abnormal temperature conditions may increasingly influence information processing in capital markets. We examine whether temperature anomalies surrounding covered firm’s headquarters are related to analysts’ earnings forecasts. Drawing on a comprehensive analyst-firm sample from 2001 to 2020, we find that greater absolute temperature anomalies are associated with significantly lower forecast optimism within [-60, 0], [-30, 0], and [-20, 0] pre-announcement windows, with the effect more pronounced for cold anomalies. Supplementary analyses suggest that abnormal local temperature conditions heighten uncertainty and are associated with more conservative earnings forecasts. Our results are robust to an alternative optimism measure, firm fixed effects, entropy-balancing designs, and placebo experiments exploiting lagged optimism. Collectively, the results indicate that temperature anomalies in the covered firm’s local environment are associated with systematic changes in analysts’ earnings forecasts and the informational environment in capital markets.

title: Inside Sales Social Media Use and Its Strategic Implications for Salesperson-Customer Digital Engagement and Performance

detail.title: Inside Sales Social Media Use and Its Strategic Implications for Salesperson-Customer Digital Engagement and Performance
detail.abstract: The nature of inside sales has shifted, increasing in autonomy, importance, and scope. Moreover, buyers are changing their preferences from face-to-face interactions to virtual-based relationships, leading to a future full of opportunities for inside salespeople using social media. The practitioner literature suggests that inside sales represent the sales business model of the digital era and a distinct strategic selling approach. While there has been a recent surge in theoretical research on inside sales, extant research fails to explore how and why inside salespeople uses social media as a critical tool. Research on social media use in sales has neglected to consider the growing role of inside sales, where sellers lack the opportunity to meet with customers face-to-face and must routinely rely on remote communication to interact with customers. As such, we use a grounded theory approach to investigate the "lived experiences" of inside salespeople at the intersection with social media in sales. Emergent from our findings is a framework depicting: inside sales strategic social media use → inside salesperson-customer digital engagement → inside sales performance. We also find that firm digital technology resources serve as enablement factors that shape the effects of the social media strategies that inside salespeople use.

title: AI-Assisted Learning: Product Strategy under Customer Heterogeneity
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN and Monash Business School, Monash University

detail.title: AI-Assisted Learning: Product Strategy under Customer Heterogeneity

publicationDetails.detailsText: No. This paper has not appeared in, nor has it been accepted for publication in, any paper series, journal, or book.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies such as generative AI are transforming how people learn, driving knowledge-service firms to add AI-assisted learning products to their product lines. Because AI technologies evolve fast, the value of these products varies across customers, and customers may not judge their own AI-usage capability properly. We develop a game-theoretic model in which a knowledge-service firm decides whether to offer an AI-assisted learning product alongside its baseline product and how to price them. The model captures two salient features in AI-assisted learning: customers differ in their AI-usage capability, and only a fraction of customers are aware of their own capability. First, we find that the firm's optimal AI product strategy takes three forms depending on the efficacy of the AI product. Within each strategy region, a higher AI efficacy raises the price of the AI product, but an efficacy gain that pushes the firm across strategy regions may lower the price. Second, customer capability heterogeneity and AI-awareness affect the firm's profit through distinct channels, and AI efficacy shapes how each effect plays out.  We further examine customers' belief bias about AI efficacy and find that a mild overestimation may improve both the firm's profit and consumer surplus. Our findings provide important managerial insights for policymakers. Promoting AI literacy improves both the firm's profit and consumer surplus when AI efficacy is low. Under high AI efficacy, however, it raises consumer surplus but can lower firm profit. We extend the model to examine the effect of an AI product that can narrow the gap in customers' baseline learning ability, and we also provide managerial insights for how AI deployment affects the firm's profit and consumer surplus.

detail.abstract: The international expansion of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS Church) has been driven by intensive proselytising activities, historically characterised by door-to-door missionary work and, more recently, reinforced through digital religious marketing. This article examines the contrast between the public image of the religion and the accessibility, prior to religious affiliation, of the historical, doctrinal, ritual, and institutional information essential for a comprehensive understanding of the religious organisation. The study adopts a qualitative, bibliographical, documentary, and historiographical approach, complemented by a case study based on the author's experience as a former member of the institution, the results of which were systematised in the book A Seita Mórmon: Danos Irreversíveis à Vida, às Famílias e à Humanidade (Narrativa de uma História Real). The analysis demonstrates that information potentially decisive for an informed decision-including matters relating to the Book of Mormon and the institution's other canonical scriptures; the conduct and teachings of Joseph Smith Jr.; temple ordinances, including proxy work on behalf of the dead; the doctrine of exaltation; Masonic influences; and significant historical and institutional controversies-is generally not presented clearly or comprehensively during the initial Progressive Revelation and the Omission of Information in the Process of Joining the LDS Church process of religious affiliation. Individuals approached through missionary proselytism or digital religious marketing are initially introduced to a message centred upon Jesus Christ, a connection reinforced by the denomination's official name, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, together with the restoration of the Church through Joseph Smith Jr., the Book of Mormon as "Another Testament of Jesus Christ", and the doctrine that families may remain united throughout eternity. At this initial stage, the distinctive features of Latter-day Saint Christology are generally not fully disclosed. By contrast, information essential to a proper understanding of the religion-and capable of substantially altering that understanding-is absent from the initial doctrinal presentations and typically becomes known only after baptism or through independent investigation. This article proposes the concept of religious information asymmetry to describe the disparity between the historical, doctrinal, ritual, and institutional information available to the religious organisation and that actually disclosed to prospective members before they decide to join. It is argued that the selective disclosure of such information, together with the manner and timing in which it reaches prospective members-most often through their own independent investigation-constitutes central elements in evaluating institutional transparency and in safeguarding a religious decision that is free, conscious, and properly informed.

title: Applied Quantitative Analysis of R.T. Erdogan's Multi-Vector Foreign Policy in 2014-2022
affiliations: and Institute of Scientific Information for Social Sciences of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INION RAS)

detail.title: Applied Quantitative Analysis of R.T. Erdogan's Multi-Vector Foreign Policy in 2014-2022
detail.abstract: The study is devoted to the applied analysis of the concept of multi-vector in the foreign policy of Recep Tayyip Erdogan during his presidency from 2014 to 2022. Türkiye's foreign policy is of particular interest to researchers. Ankara is actively involved in regional and world politics. Turkish foreign policy is characterized as multi-vector, but different approaches to the definition of Turkish multi-vector are used in scientific research. The purpose of the study is to identify the main vectors of R.T. Erdogan's personal diplomacy during his presidency. The relevance of the work lies in the application of a quantitative method that allows identifying the main vectors of R.T. Erdogan's foreign policy on the basis of the collected database of his foreign policy contacts. The method is different in that it is free from the influence of the researcher's personal preferences in analyzing foreign policy and the influence of individual high-profile, but isolated events. The database covers the entire period of the presidency of R.T. Erdogan from 2014 to the end of 2022 and includes all foreign policy contacts published on the website of the President of Türkiye. The developed methodology allows not only to see the main vectors of foreign policy, but also to assess their depth on the basis of mathematical calculations. As a result of the analysis, the main macroregional vectors and countries in each of the vectors were identified, and the depth and quality of contacts with these countries were measured and presented. It was also found that the Turkish President actively interacts with the local level of government. Moreover, he implements the diplomacy of the second track. It covers the main macro-regional vectors from the side of public diplomacy. The database and the method allow us to assert that the policy of the Turkish president is indeed multi-vector, but the multi-vector nature of this policy is much deeper and goes beyond relations with countries. During the work, promising areas for future theoretical and applied research were identified.

title: Elastic Geometries of Choice A Metabolically Gated Quantum-Like Framework for Consumer Decision-Making

detail.title: Elastic Geometries of Choice A Metabolically Gated Quantum-Like Framework for Consumer Decision-Making

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial, professional, institutional, or personal relationships that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, the development or presentation of this work
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a conceptual and theoretical paper and did not involve human participants, animals, personal data, clinical data, or the collection of empirical data. Consequently, ethics committee approval and informed consent were not required
declarations.funderStatement: The paper presents an independent conceptual and theoretical contribution and received no specific funding from public, commercial, or not-for-profit organisations

detail.abstract: Consumer preferences are often constructed in context rather than retrieved as fixed values. Quantum-like models capture this contextuality through Hilbert-space representations, non-commutative measurements, interference, and state updating. Yet these models typically treat the representational geometry as resource-independent, whereas neuroenergetic and resource-rational accounts emphasise that biological computation is constrained by limited, dynamically allocated capacity. This conceptual working paper integrates these traditions through a framework of metabolically gated quantum-like cognition. The framework does not claim that the brain is a physical quantum computer or that adenosine triphosphate literally collapses a mental wave function. Instead, it proposes that cognitive and bioenergetic resource conditions act as boundary constraints on the effective accessibility and coherence of representations described by quantum-like models. A fixed ambient Hilbert space is retained, while a resource-sensitive gate, constrained in part by metabolic capacity, modulates the contribution of representational dimensions, and a dephasing parameter modulates contextual coherence. This resolves the contradiction between geometric compression and maximal statistical mixing that arises when low-resource states are represented only as noise. The framework predicts three regimes: expanded contextual geometry under relatively abundant resources, elastic instability and heightened order sensitivity under intermediate constraint, and compressed heuristic geometry under severe constraint. Six propositions specify effects on accessibility breadth, coherence, choice complexity, order effects, heuristic reliance, and model performance. The paper develops implications for brand equity, customer journeys, digital choice architecture, and responsible personalisation, and outlines a staged research programme combining behavioural experiments, computational model comparison, autonomic and attentional measures, direct neuroenergetic validation, and topological analysis.

title: Effects of Digital Marketing Channels on Market Performance of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: The Case of Ambo, West Shewa, Ethiopia

detail.title: Effects of Digital Marketing Channels on Market Performance of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: The Case of Ambo, West Shewa, Ethiopia
detail.abstract: In the ever-changing global economy, digital marketing channel has emerged as a crucial strategy for businesses seeking to enhance their market presence, engage with customers, and promote growth. This presence and engagement have shown significant impact performance of marketing of Micro Small and Medium enterprise. The paper has included the effect of social media marketing, email marketing, content marketing and mobile marketing effects of the marketing performance of MSMEs. Both descriptive and explanatory research design has employed with the total population of 311 MSMEs sector with the employees of 1,108 from Ambo town Ethiopia. 173 of MSMEs were selected with 286 sample representatives of employees. Surveys were collected from these using five-point Likert Scale. Both descriptive and inferential statistics were analysed. The finding indicate that social media marketing has strong positive relationship with marketing performance of business enterprise and using content marketing results in increase in marketing performance of MSMEs. The researcher has recommended that using email marketing in addition to other variables will bring more profit for MSMEs.

title: Workforce Skill Mapping, Labour Misallocation, and Aggregate Productivity

detail.title: Workforce Skill Mapping, Labour Misallocation, and Aggregate Productivity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Director of Bayswater Transflow Engineering Ltd. No external funding was received.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by Bayswater Transflow Engineering Ltd.

detail.abstract: A workforce-capability-mapping technology measures each worker's demonstrated competence against codified trade standards. It converts privately unobserved capability into a verified, standards-mapped profile, and, aggregated across a firm's workers, into a firm-wide skills matrix. We treat it abstractly, as a technology that removes an information friction over the labour input, and ask, in strict micro-thenmacro order, what it does first to a firm and then to an economy. Resolving the uncertainty over what each worker can actually do improves the internal allocation of labour to tasks and lets training be aimed at verified gaps, not sprayed across a whole workforce; it also front-loads the discovery of capability. The first two channels raise measured firm productivity and are the ones that aggregate, the third is a cost-side benefit at the firm, and all are largest where existing proxies for skill are least informative. Aggregated to scale, those two channels reduce labour misallocation and raise aggregate total factor productivity, accelerate human-capital accumulation, and ease structural transformation into higher-value industry. The misallocation literature indicates the potential prize is large, tens of per cent of TFP. The United Arab Emirates, a high-income economy whose skilled workforce is overwhelmingly migrant and hired on documents, is our application; the magnitudes are illustrative and the application prospective.

title: Why Do Some Customers Browse But Never Buy? A Customer Segmentation Study Using K -Means Clustering

detail.title: Why Do Some Customers Browse But Never Buy? A Customer Segmentation Study Using K -Means Clustering
detail.abstract: Customers who browse the most spend the least. Some customers visit the website 3x more often than the biggest spenders, yet spend 12x less, a gap this paper investigates and explains. • 2,211 real customers analysed, grouped into 4 distinct segments using K-Means clustering • The biggest spenders barely browse; the biggest browsers, on the other hand, barely spend. • This points to a psychological gap between browsing and buying, and not just a spending gap.

title: Generative AI as Learning Infrastructure, Not a Shortcut

detail.title: Generative AI as Learning Infrastructure, Not a Shortcut

detail.abstract: This paper synthesizes established learning science and recent applied research to argue that generative AI functions as either a learning infrastructure or a cognitive bypass, depending entirely on how it is deployed-not on what the technology can produce. The paper introduces cognitive engagement preservation as a necessary operative design criterion: an AI deployment is pedagogically sound if it maintains or increases the learner's active processing of material, and corrosive if it eliminates the cognitive work the task was designed to require. This reframing shifts AI adoption in education from a policy-and-permission problem to a pedagogical design problem. Evidence from cognitive load theory, retrieval practice research, tutoring effectiveness studies, and emerging applied literature on structured AI assignments supports both the criterion and its implications for assessment design, institutional policy, and early learner exposure.

detail.abstract:
Purpose
The study reconstructs the historical evolution of research on dynamic capabilities (DCs), perhaps the most influential framework in contemporary strategic management for explaining how firms achieve and sustain competitive advantage. By examining its development over nearly three decades, the study aims to explain how recurring theoretical and practical challenges shaped the framework’s evolution and growing centrality within strategic-management research.

Design/methodology/approach
The study adopts a Historical Literature Review of 140 articles published between 1997 and 2026 in leading management and organization journals. The analysis combines systematic corpus construction, bibliometric structuring, reflexive thematic analysis and historical periodization to reconstruct the field’s evolution and identify major turning points.

Findings
DCs research evolved through five historical phases. Each phase emerged from the interaction between shifts in strategic-management thinking, changes in firms’ competitive environments, and unresolved questions within the DCs literature itself. Across these phases, the framework progressively expanded from an emphasis on resource reconfiguration toward a broader conception of strategic orchestration encompassing managerial capabilities, organizational renewal, ecosystem governance and environmental shaping. As this expansion unfolded, five persistent tensions became increasingly central to understanding how DCs operate: stability versus flexibility, organizational mechanisms versus managerial agency, microfoundations versus contingency, architectural integration versus causal ambiguity, and adaptation versus shaping. Rather than being resolved, these tensions were repeatedly reframed as the framework evolved across new theoretical and empirical domains.

Originality/value
This study moves beyond existing reviews that primarily synthesize contemporary perspectives on DCs. By adopting a historical lens, it explains how the framework evolved, why its core debates emerged, and how they became constitutive of its current form. Building on this reconstruction, the study develops an integrative framework that reconceptualizes dynamic capabilities as mechanisms of strategic orchestration through which firms continuously navigate and rebalance persistent strategic tensions while pursuing competitive advantage under conditions of ongoing change.

title: Salesforce Compensation and Composition in the Age of AI
affiliations: Hunan University, , Shanghai University of International Business and Economics - School of Management and National University of Singapore

detail.title: Salesforce Compensation and Composition in the Age of AI
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming how sales are produced, yet how salesforce compensation should adapt remains an open question. We develop a game-theoretic model in which a firm posts a linear compensation contract to attract and motivate sales candidates who differ in ability and outside opportunities. The contract operates along two interconnected margins: it induces effort from the hired salesperson and, through candidate self-selection, shapes the ability composition of the pool. Sales are jointly produced by human effort and AI through a constant-elasticity-of-substitution technology that encompasses two empirically relevant regimes: assistive AI that complements human selling and autonomous AI that substitutes for it. Our central equilibrium result is that the optimal commission rate is lower under both AI regimes than in the benchmark without AI. The mechanism is that AI weakens the connection between observed sales and the salesperson’s contribution, making commissions less effective on both margins: each additional unit of commission elicits less salesperson-driven output, and performance pay attracts high-ability candidates less effectively because AI narrows the output gap between strong and weak salespeople. The practical implication is that firms should not simply layer AI onto legacy compensation plans; as AI’s role grows, reliance on commission-based pay should be recalibrated.

title: Predictive Lead Scoring in B2B Marketing: A Systematic Review of Literature (2018–2025) with Practitioner Reflections from a B2B Data Engineering Marketing Context in India

detail.title: Predictive Lead Scoring in B2B Marketing: A Systematic Review of Literature (2018–2025) with Practitioner Reflections from a B2B Data Engineering Marketing Context in India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial interests, personal relationships, or competing interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it is based solely on a review and synthesis of previously published literature and does not involve human participants, animals, or identifiable personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Lead generation in B2B marketing has witnessed a paradigm shift from mass outreach with limited qualification criteria to data-driven approaches that identify high-intent prospects based on behavioral signals, engagement patterns, and intent data. This evolution has enhanced sales-marketing alignment, with marketing becoming a strategic function for attracting, nurturing, and qualifying leads before entering the pipeline. In this evolving landscape, predictive lead scoring has emerged as a critical mechanism for prioritizing prospects in complex, multi-stakeholder B2B environments, leveraging AI-based models that continuously improve predictions based on historical data and behavioral patterns-moving beyond the static limitations of manually assigned, rule-based scoring. However, despite increasing adoption by practitioners, academic literature on predictive lead scoring remains fragmented, largely B2C-oriented, and empirically limited.
This systematic review aggregates peer-reviewed and practitioner-academic literature between 2018 and 2025 to examine the impact of predictive analytics, artificial intelligence, intent data, and account-based marketing frameworks on buyer identification, lead qualification, and pipeline performance in B2B sectors such as technology, manufacturing, SaaS, and professional services. The systematic search was carried out for five major academic databases for relevant studies meeting pre-specified inclusion criteria following a PRISMA-guided protocol. 
The review identifies five major thematic clusters: (1) predictive lead scoring models and algorithms, (2) buyer and account identification, (3) intent data and behavioural signals, (4) personalisation and demand generation, (5) sales-marketing alignment. 
Results confirm that machine learning approaches, especially logistic regression, random forests and gradient boosting, consistently outperform traditional rule-based scoring in conversion accuracy. Analytics culture, data quality and CRM governance emerge as critical organisational enablers of effective implementation. This review consolidates a fragmented evidence base and highlights the organisational and technical conditions necessary for effective predictive lead scoring in B2B contexts, offering direction for both future research and practice. 
In addition, the first author’s personal experience as a marketing practitioner at a B2B data engineering firm in India, where predictive analytics and intent-data tools were implemented in live campaign and pipeline contexts, further informs this review. This practitioner perspective is employed, with the requisite degree of caution, to demonstrate how the dynamics described in the literature is manifested in daily commercial operations and reveals implementation realities, particularly 3 those related to organisational trust in algorithmic outputs, that have not yet been thoroughly documented in secondary academic reviews. There are substantial research voids that persist in the areas of SME contexts, emerging economies, longitudinal model performance, explainable AI adoption, and the integration of generative AI with predictive scoring systems. This review identifies a prioritised agenda for future empirical research in predictive B2B marketing intelligence and establishes a consolidated conceptual foundation.

title: Socially Necessary Participation: A Theory of the Pre-production Conditions of Economic Value
affiliations: and

detail.title: Socially Necessary Participation: A Theory of the Pre-production Conditions of Economic Value
detail.abstract:
Economic theory provides influential explanations of productive capabilities, production, institutions, and technological change. The correspondence between individual productive capabilities and the productive resources through which production is organized, however, has received comparatively limited explicit theoretical attention. Existing approaches explain how productive capabilities are developed, how production is organized, and how institutions shape economic performance, but generally treat participation as an analytical presupposition rather than an object of inquiry.

This paper develops the theory of Socially Necessary Participation (SNP), which conceptualizes participation as a distinct analytical stage preceding production. The framework distinguishes between the Means of Participation, defined as the capabilities, attributes, and conditions individuals bring to production, and the Means of Production, comprising the physical, technological, financial, organizational, institutional, and material resources through which production is organized and carried out. Socially Necessary Participation is defined as the pre-production correspondence between the Means of Participation and the Means of Production. The extent of this correspondence conditions the extent to which productive capabilities are translated into realized economic value.

By distinguishing analytically between possessing productive capabilities and realizing their economic value, the framework complements classical political economy, human capital theory, institutional economics, and development economics without displacing their core insights. It provides a general analytical framework for explaining why individuals possessing comparable productive capabilities may nevertheless realize different levels of economic value, or remain unable to realize their productive potential, under different technological, organizational, institutional, and material conditions.

title: Cumulonimbus Cloud System and Indigenous Spirituality: A Comparative Semiotic Theology of Convective Storms in the Anthropocene

detail.title: Cumulonimbus Cloud System and Indigenous Spirituality: A Comparative Semiotic Theology of Convective Storms in the Anthropocene
detail.abstract: Across widely separated cosmological traditions, the cumulonimbus cloud, towering, dark-based, and anvil-crowned, functions less as inert atmospheric phenomenon than as a legible text through which communities read divine presence, moral order, and ecological reciprocity. This study offers a comparative theological and semiotic analysis of storm cosmology across Yoruba, Andean, Aboriginal Australian, Algonquian and Siouan, Māori, and Vedic traditions, arguing that convective morphology, cumulus genesis, mature electrification, dissipative collapse, has historically supplied a narrative armature for cosmological meaning. Drawing on Peircean semiotics, a relationally revised hierophany, and ontologies from the anthropology of nature, the study proposes a model termed convective theophany, reading the storm's three-stage cycle isomorphically against ritual emergence, threat, and resolution. It distinguishes cases where cellscale morphology is the direct theological referent from cases operating at monsoon or system scale, treating this as a finding, not a complication, and separates the framework's falsifiable structural claim from its modest typology of adaptive strategies. The study examines how anthropogenic climate change destabilizes these semiotic economies at the level of referential content while leaving formal structure intact, prompting reinterpretation or reconstitution of cosmological frameworks, and closes by proposing a vocabulary for climate communication scholarship attentive to cosmological plurality and its evidentiary limits.

title: Sectoral Frontier Decompositions and the Tradables Margin: Mix Efficiency, Manufacturing, and the Limits of Slack
affiliations: Northeastern University and

detail.title: Sectoral Frontier Decompositions and the Tradables Margin: Mix Efficiency, Manufacturing, and the Limits of Slack

declarations.funderStatement: There are no financial interests to disclose.

detail.abstract: Manufacturing converges unconditionally while aggregate economies do not, so a world frontier estimated on aggregate output mismeasures the sector where catch-up lives; yet shift-share sectoral accounting has no technology benchmark, and the efficiency toolkit lacks exact structure beyond one output. For one input and m outputs we prove three results. Tone's slacks-based measure equals observed average productivity-in a scalarization weighted by the observation's own inverse outputs-relative to the best attainable with no more input and no less of any output, and factors exactly into the Farrell radial score times a mixslack term, sharpening Tone's inequality to an identity and giving output-mix efficiency a closed characterization. Relaxing componentwise to scalar dominance collapses the m-output measure, exactly, to the known single-output closed form on scalarized data: a certified LP-free bound, exact on a characterizable regime, that transfers the entire single-output theory along output rays. And no factorization with slack depending only on the input and the output mix exists, by an analytic three-point counterexample with closed-form σ(t). We then build the two-output (manufacturing/non-manufacturing) world frontier for 139 countries, 1970-2020, and audit its headline association: manufacturing trade balances predicting movement toward the sectoral frontier, invisible to the aggregate frontier. The association survives outlier-robust order-m frontiers and influential-country deletion, and fails the two audits the parent literatures demand-constant-price output splits flip its sign, and the frontier-re-estimating cluster bootstrap spans zero. The factorization then locates the fragility: mix slack is pervasive and concentrated in manufacturing-heavy economies; the slacks-based measure is null on the manufacturing balance because its radial and mix components cancel; and the cross-deflator correlation is 0.45 for the mix margin against 0.83 for the radial score. The theorems are the durable contribution; the application shows both how much discipline sectoral frontier inference requires and what exact structure buys-the ability to see where the fragility lives.

title: Extended Johnson's Rules for Flow Shop Scheduling with Category-Dependent Learning and Forgetting Effects
affiliations: and Beijing Institute of Technology - School of Management and Economics

detail.title: Extended Johnson's Rules for Flow Shop Scheduling with Category-Dependent Learning and Forgetting Effects

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors reported no potential conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: Motivated by operations at a large-scale personal computer manufacturing factory assembly line, we investigate a flow shop scheduling problem with category-dependent learning and forgetting effects (CLFEs), where workers' proficiency affects processing efficiency. First, we propose a general CLFEs model to characterize the monotonicity between proficiency and efficiency, including existing specific learning curve formulations as special cases. Second, for the twomachine scheduling problem, we propose a Batch-wise Johnson's (BJ) rule to construct an optimal batch-wise schedule (i.e., a schedule where jobs of the same category are processed consecutively), which extends the well-known Johnson's rule. Next, we establish optimal scheduling rules for three specific two-machine scheduling scenarios: for problems with a strong forgetting effect, we prove the global optimality of the BJ rule; for problems without a forgetting effect, we propose an optimal partition-based Johnson's rule; for general two-machine scheduling problems, we provide sufficient conditions for the optimality of the BJ rule. Finally, for general multi-machine scheduling problems, we develop a Multi-machine Batch-wise Johnson's (MBJ) algorithm based on the principles of the BJ rule. Numerical studies show that the BJ rule for the two-machine scheduling problem is nearly optimal with an average optimality gap of 0.1%, and the MBJ algorithm finds nearly optimal batch-wise schedules for all multi-machine instances. Furthermore, our computational results reveal that the average optimal makespan gap between problems with and without CLFEs is approximately 10%, highlighting the practical importance of considering CLFEs in production planning.

title: Copyrighting Style? Reframing Style Imitation as Non-Literal Copying in EU Copyright Law: Implications for Generative AI and Fashion Dupes

detail.title: Copyrighting Style? Reframing Style Imitation as Non-Literal Copying in EU Copyright Law: Implications for Generative AI and Fashion Dupes
detail.abstract:
The proposition that artistic style falls outside copyright protection is widely regarded as axiomatic in copyright law. Under the idea/expression dichotomy, authors may claim exclusive rights over the specific expression of their ideas, but not over artistic styles, genres or aesthetic vocabulary. Recent developments, however, have made the copyright treatment of style increasingly difficult to ignore. Generative artificial intelligence can produce works in the recognisable style of individual creators within seconds, while fashion dupes systematically reproduce the aesthetic language of successful luxury designs without literal copying. These developments have prompted renewed interest in the relationship between copyright and artistic style.

This article argues that the central question has been framed too broadly. The issue is not whether copyright should protect style itself. Rather, it is whether conduct described as “style imitation” may already constitute the non-literal reproduction of protected expression under existing EU copyright law. Revisiting the Court of Justice’s jurisprudence on originality and the reproduction right, the article demonstrates that the existing framework already provides the doctrinal tools necessary to distinguish between lawful stylistic inspiration and copyright infringement. It concludes that AI-generated outputs and fashion dupes do not expose a need to copyright style, but rather a need to recognise more clearly when apparent stylistic borrowing is, in reality, the non-literal reproduction of protected expression.

title: Who Leads When No One Is in Control? A Systems Thinking Approach to Navigating Complexity in European Population Health, Conflict and Hybrid Crises
affiliations: , Schloss Leopoldskron, King’s College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and State Health Office

detail.title: Who Leads When No One Is in Control? A Systems Thinking Approach to Navigating Complexity in European Population Health, Conflict and Hybrid Crises

declarations.declarationOfInterest: MR, MHP, DB, and AW report no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This article is a conceptual paper. It does not report human participant research, evaluate the Sciana program, analyze individual-level workshop data, or include direct quotations, identifiable information or attributable participant contributions. Fellows join Sciana through a voluntary application and selection process. The workshop is used only as a reflective leadership-development context and as a source of non-attributable, aggregated themes that informed the authors’ conceptual argument. For these reasons, formal research ethics approval and informed consent for research participation were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: Sciana: The Health Leaders Network covered travel and accommodation costs for fellows attending the workshop on which this conceptual paper draws. The authors received no specific financial support for the authorship, analysis, interpretation or preparation of this manuscript.

detail.abstract:
Purpose: Europe's security environment is changing faster than most health systems have adapted: conflict, hybrid threats, cyber disruption, supply-chain failure and population movement can produce rapid health consequences before presenting as conventional health emergencies. This conceptual paper develops a systems-leadership framing for conflict preparedness when no single actor controls the whole system. 
Design/methodology/approach: The paper draws on a Sciana Health Leaders Network workshop in Salzburg with Cohorts 7 and 8, using a conflict and hybrid-crisis scenario and German-centered input on federalism, civil-military cooperation and Germany's transit, supply and coordination role. 
Findings: Conflict and hybrid crises expose population health as a distributed responsibility. Health systems depend on hidden infrastructure: power, water, transport, digital networks, supply chains, staff availability, social care and public trust. Scarcity becomes ethically hazardous when resource prioritization is opaque, implicit or driven by operational convenience. Marginalized groups may become invisible unless leaders build population visibility and community intelligence. Civil-military health cooperation must be built before it is tested. Key preparedness assets include relationships, shared language, trust, transparent decision logs and practiced adaptation mechanisms. Preparedness requires institutional capacity and community agency; resilience grows when people understand their role and can contribute. 
Originality: The paper reframes conflict preparedness as a systems-leadership challenge for health services, viewed through a population health lens. It argues that leadership is tested not by whether one organization performs well, but whether many organizations can create fairness, trust and continuity among themselves when no single actor controls the system.

title: Note on Identification of Forward-looking Stockpiling Models
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School, University of Toronto at Mississauga - Department of Management and

detail.title: Note on Identification of Forward-looking Stockpiling Models
detail.abstract: This note clarifies the identification of a stockpiling model when consumers are forwardlooking. We first emphasize that price can be constant in a stockpiling model, as the inventory state variable alone is sufficient to generate dynamic behavior. We then show that a stockpiling model naturally satisfies 1-period finite dependence, which can be combined with a single exclusion restriction to uniquely identify the discount factor. We further demonstrate that the remaining structural parameters of the model can be identified. Furthermore, we provide deeper intuition regarding the commonly used difference in log choice probabilities equation when choice probabilities are not completely substituted for value functions. Finally, we compare our finite dependence property with that used in Abbring and Daljord (2020).

title: International Models of Small-business Competitiveness Support: A Comparative Analysis and Lessons for an Emerging Economy

detail.title: International Models of Small-business Competitiveness Support: A Comparative Analysis and Lessons for an Emerging Economy
detail.abstract: Emerging economies increasingly seek to raise the competitiveness of their small-business sector, yet the choice of policy model is rarely grounded in comparative evidence. This paper analyses five influential national models of small-business competitiveness support-Germany's Mittelstand and KfW system, South Korea's public-private TIPS architecture, Singapore's sector-specific digital transformation, the market-based multi-channel system of the United States, and China's 'specialised, refined, distinctive, innovative' (Zhuanjingtexin) certification model-and extracts principles applicable to Uzbekistan. Using a structured qualitative comparison organised around three mechanism groups (financial, market and institutional), the study finds that success in every case rests on the systemic combination of the three mechanisms rather than on any single instrument, that results-measurement systems are a common feature of the more adaptable models, and that direct transplantation fails without adaptation to national capacity. On this basis, six transferable principles are proposed for Uzbekistan, including stage-specific financing, public-private selection, sector-specific digital roadmaps, a public-procurement set-aside, and specialisation-based certification. The paper contributes a comparative framework linking mechanism design to measurable outcomes for small-business policy in transition settings.

title: Alternative Marine Fuel Quality as the Legal Foundation of Post-bunkering Disputes

detail.title: Alternative Marine Fuel Quality as the Legal Foundation of Post-bunkering Disputes
detail.abstract: This arcticle examines the quality of alternative marine fuel as the starting point for disputes arising after bunkering. As shipping increasingly relies on liquefied natural gas, methanol, biofuels, synthetic fuels, and renewable blends, legal analysis should begin by identifying the substance supplied, determining whether it complied with the agreed specification at the point of custody transfer, and establishing how representative samples were taken, preserved, and tested. It must also distinguish defects existing at delivery from changes caused by onboard storage, mixing, conditioning, or use. Drawing on ISO standards, IMO materials, BIMCO forms, Gard guidance, Russian sales and technical-regulation rules, and marine-engineering literature, the article argues that fuel quality is a distinct contractual and evidentiary issue rather than a technical appendix to broader claims concerning pollution, physical damage, or operational casualties. It proposes a “quality file” as a structured model for contract drafting, evidence preservation, causation analysis, and claims handling in transactions involving alternative marine fuels.

title: Title: rganizational Immunity, Emotional Exhaustion, and Perceived Performance in the Libyan Healthcare Sector: A Mixed-Methods Study​
affiliations: Libyan Authority for Scientific Research

detail.title: Title: rganizational Immunity, Emotional Exhaustion, and Perceived Performance in the Libyan Healthcare Sector: A Mixed-Methods Study​
detail.abstract: Contrary to five decades of burnout research, this study finds emotional exhaustion does not significantly predict performance decline among 5,000 healthcare workers surveyed across five Libyan cities, despite daily 12-18 hour power cuts (2016-2021), armed militias demanding treatment at gunpoint, and a 2023 salary law fixing experienced nurses' wages below 400 USD while parliamentarians earned over 4,000 USD.This finding led us to reframe the question: what enables a healthcare organization to keep functioning when its environment collapses? Building on Conservation of Resources theory, the dynamic capabilities view, and organizational resilience research, we propose organizational immunity: an institution's capacity to detect threats, mobilize responses, and codify learning. We tested it via a mixed-methods design combining the survey with interviews of 25 senior managers, treating the hospital as one interdependent system.Organizational immunity substantially enhanced perceived performance (β = 0.42, p < 0.001) and reduced exhaustion even more strongly (β = −0.51, p < 0.001), while exhaustion's effect on performance was non-significant (β = −0.18, p = 0.085): staff kept performing regardless, as one head nurse put it, because she cannot afford to feel tired while twenty patients are waiting.We also document how UNDP solar installations in 15 hospitals since 2017 improved electricity reliability, yet workers still faced gunpoint demands and pay a fraction of parliamentarians'. We distinguish fragile innate immunity from durable, system-encoded acquired immunity, and offer a low-cost, four-step framework for building organizational immunity in fragile settings.

title: SANOS-Evolve: A Discrete Stochastic-local-volatility Model for European-option Smile Dynamics

detail.title: SANOS-Evolve: A Discrete Stochastic-local-volatility Model for European-option Smile Dynamics
detail.abstract: An arbitrage-free set of option marginals fixes an underlying's local-volatility content, but not how its smile moves when the spot moves. Existing models are either parametric in the smile (stochastic volatility) or exact but expensive to calibrate (stochastic-local volatility). SANOS-Evolve keeps the two separate: a static SANOS linear program fixes strictly arbitrage-free marginals, and a dynamic layer fits a martingale two-timescale kernel between them, calibrated while the marginals stay fixed and arbitrage-free by construction (Strassen). Every object is a Gaussian mixture, so prices, Greeks, and the variance-index smile are closed-form. Translation invariance makes the skew-stickiness ratio an exact closed-form realised covariance whose term structure the two timescales fit, and identifies the vol-of-vol from a forward-variance readout-VIX for SPX, the strip's own curvature otherwise. One calibrated object yields the surface, exotics, and SSR-consistent hedges; on SPX the delta reproduces the industry Hull-White minimum-variance benchmark from the smile alone, with no trailing realised estimate.

title:
The Rollout of Public Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicles in the Netherlands: Innovation and Infrastructure

An Ex-Post Analysis
affiliations: Wageningen University

detail.title:
The Rollout of Public Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicles in the Netherlands: Innovation and Infrastructure

An Ex-Post Analysis
detail.abstract: Accelerating the impact of transformative climate change mitigation policies (TCCMP) requires a timely evaluation of current policies. Evaluating such policies poses a number of challenges. This paper presents a framework to evaluate individual TCCMPs by combining elements from the Technological Innovation Systems (TIS) literature and the literature on TCCMPs. The framework is used to assess Dutch public policies for the rollout of (semi)public charging infrastructure for electric vehicles in the period 2009-2020 using document studies and expert interviews. During this period the Netherlands became a clear frontrunner in high quality public charging infrastructure. The experts identified 61 obstacles that were encountered and, in their opinion, policies of the central government contributed to solving about half (29) of them. These obstacles and the policies used to solve them are structured using the new Adjusted-TIS framework and the linear innovation model. The results suggest that the policies of the central government are insufficient to understand the rapid rollout of (semi)public charging infrastructure in the Netherlands. Large municipalities and a foundation called Elaad were at least as important.

title: Collaborating Across Time Zones -digital Platforms, Asynchronous Practices, and Performance in Global Virtual Teams

detail.title: Collaborating Across Time Zones -digital Platforms, Asynchronous Practices, and Performance in Global Virtual Teams
detail.abstract: Global virtual teams in multinational enterprises increasingly operate with minimal timezone overlap, which often creates structural constraints for communication and coordination. This study examines how the perceived effectiveness of digital collaboration platforms is associated with collaborative performance in remote-first, tech-enabled HR professional service firms operating under high temporal dispersion and limited time-zone overlap, and explores the asynchronous practices that support collaboration in culturally diverse global virtual teams. A mixed-methods design was used, combining cross-sectional survey data from 167 remote-working employees across 45 countries with thematic analysis of open-ended responses. Quantitative results show a strong positive association between perceived platform effectiveness and collaborative performance. Qualitative findings identify recurring practices that enable collaboration under limited overlap, including structured documentation, threaded discussions, lightweight recorded updates, interoperability across communication and task systems, and visibility into colleagues' time zones. The findings suggest that, in low time-zone overlap settings, effective collaboration depends less on default reliance on synchronous rich media and more on the flexible use of written, audio, and visual channels matched to task and temporal constraints. The study contributes to understanding how collaboration technologies support performance under conditions of limited time-zone overlap in remote-first global work and offers practical guidance for designing digital tool ecosystems, documentation standards, and time-zone-aware coordination routines.

title: The Power of "Made in Italy": How Country of Origin Shapes Global Consumer Perception and Brand Value

detail.title: The Power of "Made in Italy": How Country of Origin Shapes Global Consumer Perception and Brand Value
detail.abstract: This research paper analyzes how the "Made in Italy" label shapes global consumer perceptions, contributing to the creation of brand equity and competitive advantage in international markets. In an increasingly competitive global economy, understanding how a brand's country of origin enhances consumer valuation has become critical for strategic differentiation. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach, this study combines a literature review with primary survey results and four comparative case studies: Ferrari, Riva, Golden Goose, and San Pellegrino. The findings indicate that the "Made in Italy" label functions as a strategic intangible asset rather than a mere geographical indicator, driving long-term sustainable competitive advantage in international markets.

title: Child Trafficking: A Global Overview and Statistical Analysis

detail.title: Child Trafficking: A Global Overview and Statistical Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with any people or organizations that could have influenced, or be perceived to have influenced, this research paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or primary data collection, and therefore did not require ethics committee approval or informed consent. All data used are drawn from publicly available secondary sources (UNODC, ILO, Walk Free, and IOM reports).
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agency.

detail.abstract: Child trafficking remains one of the most severe violations of children's rights in the contemporary world, encompassing sexual exploitation, forced labour, forced marriage, forced criminality, and other forms of coercive exploitation. Drawing on the most recent data published by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), the International Labour Organization (ILO), Walk Free, and the International Organization for Migration (IOM), this paper presents a global overview of the scale, distribution, and trajectory of child trafficking between 2019 and 2024. It examines the definitional and legal framework established by the Palermo Protocol, analyses regional variation in prevalence and typology, considers the structural drivers of vulnerability, and reviews the current state of prevention and protection efforts. The evidence indicates that detected child trafficking has increased substantially in recent years, driven by intersecting pressures of poverty, armed conflict, climate-related displacement, and the growth of technology-facilitated exploitation, and that response systems in most regions remain under-resourced relative to the scale of the problem.

title:
Financial Literacy as Provident Infrastructure
Savings Capacity, Monetary Agency, and the Reproduction of Development
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
Financial Literacy as Provident Infrastructure
Savings Capacity, Monetary Agency, and the Reproduction of Development
detail.abstract: Financial literacy is commonly treated as an individual stock of knowledge or a set of behaviours associated with budgeting, saving, borrowing, and product choice. This article argues that the individual-skill model is necessary but incomplete for development theory. It reconceptualises financial literacy as provident infrastructure: a distributed capacity through which societies reproduce monetary agency across households, institutions, and generations. The article makes three distinctions. First, monetary agency is not reducible to knowledge; it emerges when interpretive competence is converted into usable choice under conditions of material room, institutional intelligibility, protection, and redress. Second, savings capacity is not the same as observed saving; it concerns whether households can preserve value after dignified basic needs and unavoidable obligations, given income volatility, inflation, fees, shocks, and the safety of available instruments. Third, access to finance is not equivalent to inclusion quality or agency. The article positions these claims against financial literacy, financial capability, financial well-being, financial fragility, and family financial socialisation, and develops transformative economic memory as a wider transmission system linking content, carriers, decision occasions, and feedback. A rights-first account recognises foundational literacy, numeracy, language, disability, oral and group-based knowledge, and the right to protection regardless of competence. Artificial intelligence is treated as a bounded extension: voice, translation, and explanation may widen access, but assisted task completion can become synthetic financial literacy when users do not retain comprehension or authorship. The article proposes a Provident Financial Capability framework, four testable propositions, remedy zones identifying when education is and is not the principal intervention, and indicators for the Providence Value Unit. Its central claim is relational: development cannot be reproduced by teaching people to navigate systems that leave them no room to act or no institution answerable for the consequences.

title: Tribal Sovereignty, Decolonization, and Abolition: Why Tribes Should Reconsider Punishment

detail.title: Tribal Sovereignty, Decolonization, and Abolition: Why Tribes Should Reconsider Punishment
detail.abstract: This Comment outlines the intersections of abolition theory and decolonization theory, and then proposes that Tribal Nations become leaders in reconsidering systems of punishment and instead create systems of care and liberation. It argues that because abolition is a decolonial project, tribes should adopt abolitionist practices in their own communities. Part I provides an overview of the history of incarceration and policing of Indigenous peoples. Part II maps out what tribal sovereignty and criminal jurisdiction currently looks like for Tribal Nations today. Part III analyzes abolition theory and decolonization theory, its intersections, and how the goals of abolition meet the goals of decolonization. Lastly, Part IV lays out a proposal for why and how tribes can replace the current criminal legal system modeled after the U.S. carceral system in their communities with tribal restorative and transformative justice systems, becoming a leader for the rest of the United States.

title: Choice Under Constraint: Enterprise-Fund Transfers and Divergent Fiscal Trajectories Among Virginia's Independent Cities
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Choice Under Constraint: Enterprise-Fund Transfers and Divergent Fiscal Trajectories Among Virginia's Independent Cities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests and no financial or contractual relationship with the City of Radford, the City of Martinsville, their councils or staffs, or the Virginia Auditor of Public Accounts.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no financial support for the research, authorship, or preparation of this working paper.

detail.abstract: Among structurally similar Virginia independent cities, the evidence is consistent with the proposition that a sustained discretionary interfund transfer, alongside shared structural pressure, materially reduced one city's fiscal margin of safety. Radford's total net position fell 35 percent over FY2015-FY2024 while three peer cities grew theirs 40 to 67 percent. Radford moved municipal electric-utility margin into its general fund at 18.5 percent of operating revenue, against a zero-to-seven percent observed peer range, drawing a cumulative $52.04 million from FY2011 through FY2024; a closely matched comparison city running a broadly similar utility at a similar scale, but transferring nothing, stayed solvent. Audited proprietary-fund statements show Radford's electric-fund working capital falling from $9.9 million in FY2015 to negative $2.3 million in FY2024 as the transfers persisted. Using a nested comparative-case design built entirely from audited financial reports, the paper treats the transfer as a recurring budget mechanism and a material, temporally prior contributor to that deterioration, consistent with fiscal illusion. It offers a transfer-to-operating-revenue ratio as a candidate monitoring screen that aggregate distress measures can miss.

title: Continuity as an Institutional Objective: Rethinking the Purpose of Financial Infrastructure

detail.title: Continuity as an Institutional Objective: Rethinking the Purpose of Financial Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the research presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is theoretical and does not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Financial infrastructure has traditionally been evaluated through measures such as efficiency, liquidity, scalability, resilience, and transaction costs. These criteria have shaped the design of payment systems, capital markets, custody arrangements, and institutional governance for decades. Yet they share a common assumption: that the primary purpose of infrastructure is to facilitate economic activity as efficiently as possible. This paper argues that this assumption has become increasingly inadequate. In an environment characterised by geopolitical fragmentation, technological disruption, jurisdictional competition, and intergenerational wealth transfer, the central challenge is no longer the optimisation of transactions but the preservation of institutional continuity. Continuity is proposed as an independent objective of institutional design rather than a secondary consequence of resilience or governance. Unlike resilience, which focuses on recovery after disruption, continuity concerns the uninterrupted preservation of legal authority, ownership, settlement finality, institutional memory, and decision-making capacity across time and structural change. The paper develops a conceptual framework for continuity-centred infrastructure and identifies its principal dimensions, including governance continuity, ownership continuity, settlement continuity, jurisdictional continuity, historical continuity, and decision continuity. It further examines the implications of treating continuity as a design objective for financial institutions, family offices, trust structures, and long-term asset protection. The argument advanced is that mature financial infrastructures ultimately evolve beyond transaction processing. Their defining function becomes the preservation of institutional coherence across generations, technologies, and jurisdictions. In this sense, continuity represents not merely an operational characteristic but the fundamental objective around which future institutional architecture should be designed.

reference: Production and Operations Management, volume 33, issue 4, 2024[10.1177/10591478241238970]
title: Managing Replenishment and Clearance of Perishables: LIFO Issuing Policy and Age-Sensitive Demand
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management (IIMB), Bangalore and Indian Institute of Management (IIMB), Bangalore

detail.title: Managing Replenishment and Clearance of Perishables: LIFO Issuing Policy and Age-Sensitive Demand

publicationDetails.detailsText: Production and Operations Management, volume 33, issue 4, 2024[10.1177/10591478241238970]

detail.abstract: In supermarkets, customers choose the unit(s) they purchase, which leads to inventory being sold in a last-in, first-out (LIFO) order for perishable products.  Further, for such products, the demand for inventory may depend on its age since customers may choose to walk away if the freshest available inventory is too old for them.  Despite widespread occurrence of LIFO-based inventory systems, few studies have analyzed them.  In this study, we contribute by developing insights on joint replenishment and clearance policy for a perishable product with a general, finite lifetime using a periodic review model such that the inventory is sold in a LIFO order and demand is age-dependent. The model seeks to optimize two decisions every period: how much of fresh inventory to order and how much of existing inventory to clear. A key objective of the model is to understand the effect of age-dependence of demand on the optimal replenishment and clearance policy. We find that the optimal clearance policy for all but the oldest inventory is a multi-index policy such that between any pair of adjacent indexes, either no inventory is cleared or all the inventory is cleared till the lower index.  For the oldest inventory, we show that the optimal policy may have multiple forms depending upon how sensitive demand is to inventory's age.  This is a notable result in inventory theory since parameters usually affect only the policy value(s) and not the policy structure. Since the optimal policy has a complex structure in general, which makes it difficult to compute, we develop an efficient heuristic to compute the replenishment and clearance quantities. The heuristic underperforms the optimal policy by approximately 0.92% on average.

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to enhance CONSOB's enforcement against unauthorised financial activities
affiliations: University of Salerno, CONSOB (Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa), CONSOB (Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa) and CONSOB (Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa)

detail.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to enhance CONSOB's enforcement against unauthorised financial activities
detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the most significant contemporary technological innovations, with a substantial and far-reaching impact across all sectors, including the financial sector. This study explores the use of AI in combating financial fraud through the use of software developed by CONSOB in collaboration with the Polytechnic University of Turin and the Polytechnic University of the Marche. The study focuses on the use of specific AI technologies, such as Large Language Models (LLMs) and Natural Language Processing (NLP), highlighting their role in analysing, extracting, and processing the information contained in complaints filed by investors, as well as in analysing the websites of the entities reported.

This paper describes the development of the prototype in question, which integrates techniques based on hybrid artificial intelligence, with a particular focus on the accuracy and robustness of information extraction from available content.

The evaluation of the system’s results was conducted by comparing the system’s outputs with those derived from an analyst’s review, with particular attention to the accuracy, coherence, and consistency of the generated responses. In particular, the results highlight the potential of AI in automating complex financial supervision processes, while acknowledging its current limitations. In fact, the article describes the inherent limitations of current AI technologies, such as handling semantic complexity and the explainability of LLMs, highlighting key areas for optimisation to facilitate future improvements.

Building on the prototype examined, the study ultimately offers a broader reflection on the technical and organisational implications and the legal framework governing the use of AI in supervisory processes, with particular attention to human oversight, traceability, accountability, and compliance with the AI Act and national regulations.

With specific reference to the issue of human supervision, it is important to note that the tested system does not, under any circumstances, make decisions autonomously: the software’s intervention is limited to the preliminary and preparatory phases, following a human-in-the-loop approach in which the evaluation, the final decision, and the associated responsibility remain with the operator. In fact, the system provides that, through a feedback mechanism, the operator can evaluate and, if necessary, modify the results produced by the software, both in terms of the final outcome and with regard to the extraction of specific information gathered during the various stages of analysing the complaints and websites.

title: The Shared Discovery Paradox How a One-Answer Rule Turns Better Information into Worse Search

detail.title: The Shared Discovery Paradox How a One-Answer Rule Turns Better Information into Worse Search
detail.abstract: Organizations often pool dispersed information into one ranking and then allow many agents to act on that shared view. In a discovery problem, this can improve beliefs while reducing coverage. We develop an exactly solvable benchmark with sixteen boxes, one target, eight searchers, and noisy private clues. Pooling raises the accuracy of the best single recommendation from 0.20 to 0.3835, but repeating that recommendation lowers group discovery from 0.8322 under decentralized clue-following to 0.3835. A coordinated eight-action portfolio using the same pooled reports reaches 0.8594, and seven coordinated actions recover the decentralized benchmark. The paradox is not an information failure. It is a protocol failure: a one-answer rule compresses a portfolio of available actions into one repeated choice. We then replace the planner with self-interested searchers who split a prize. The equal-split game is a potential game. Its anonymous symmetric equilibrium obeys a water-filling rule, and discovery equals N times the common equilibrium payoff. In the canonical instance it achieves 0.5991: strictly above consensus, but below both private search and the planner. The exact mixed price of anarchy is 2-1/N, while uniform symmetric mixing yields the familiar e/(e-1) limit. A sole-rescue reward, which pays only an agent who covers the target alone, makes every pure Nash equilibrium first-best. Finally, a latent common-cue model shows how correlated reports collapse effective discovery channels. The centralized planner gain rises strictly with copying, and in the canonical environment the symmetric market overtakes decentralized report-following at copying probability c = 0.788462. In a proportional large-market limit the five-protocol ordering survives exactly: consensus discovery vanishes while blind, market, private, and portfolio search converge to 0.500, 0.547, 0.847, and 0.874. The contribution is a compact benchmark that separates information, allocation, incentives, and dependence into exact, reusable quantities.

title: When Markets Move as One: Institutional Synchronization after Trading Halts -Evidence from Korea's 2026 Halt Cluster

detail.title: When Markets Move as One: Institutional Synchronization after Trading Halts -Evidence from Korea's 2026 Halt Cluster
detail.abstract:
Do market-wide trading halts stabilize financial markets, or do they amplify market-wide stress once trading resumes?
