This paper addresses this question using an unprecedented sequence of nine institutional trading halts implemented by the Korea Exchange (KRX) between March and July 2026, including seven market-wide circuit breakers and two index-futures sidecars. Unlike prior studies that examine isolated halt events, the clustered nature of the 2026 Korean episode provides a rare opportunity to study repeated institutional interventions within a common regulatory regime while market conditions evolve rapidly.

Using high-frequency intraday data covering more than 2,400 listed firms, together with index, ETF, options-implied volatility, and cross-market information, we examine how trading halts affect realized volatility, cross-market transmission, dynamic dependence, and cross-sectional synchronization. Our identification strategy combines event-time comparisons, high-frequency volatility measures, dynamic correlation models, placebo tests, structural-break analysis, and international falsification exercises.

We document four main findings. First, trading halts are followed by significantly higher realized volatility for Korea’s dominant semiconductor firms rather than lower post-halt volatility, indicating that reopening does not immediately stabilize trading conditions. Second, directional volatility transmission shifts sharply during halt episodes, with shocks originating from the broader KOSDAQ market propagating toward large-cap semiconductor firms, while the reverse channel remains weak. Third, cross-sectional dispersion across KOSPI 200 constituents contracts substantially despite dramatically higher aggregate volatility, suggesting that institutional trading concentrates market-wide risk into a common systematic component. Finally, every halt occurs when options markets have already priced extreme uncertainty, with event-day VKOSPI reaching the upper tail of its historical distribution.

Taken together, the evidence is consistent with the Institutional Synchronization Framework (ISF) developed in this paper. We formalize the ISF as a two-period rational-expectations model in which institutional investors are subject to value-at-risk and margin constraints while retail investors trade on heterogeneous private information. Building on the funding-liquidity framework of Brunnermeier and Pedersen (2009), the model embeds an explicit halt-and-reopen mechanism and yields closed-form comparative statics for each empirical proposition. Under the ISF, trading halts are implemented after market stress has already become systemic and reopening mechanisms fail to dissipate aggregate uncertainty. We interpret the joint behavior of realized volatility, correlations, spillovers, dispersion, and options-implied volatility as complementary manifestations of institutional synchronization: common risk-management constraints translate heterogeneous security-specific information into homogeneous institutional trading behavior, temporarily reorganizing the architecture of market risk. Rather than viewing circuit breakers solely as volatility-control devices, our findings suggest that they may function as institutional coordination events during episodes of severe market stress. These findings contribute to the literature on market microstructure, volatility transmission, and regulatory intervention by proposing the ISF and providing new evidence from the first clustered sequence of market-wide trading halts observed in a major developed Asian equity market.

title: Sovereign Asset Party: An Analytical Framework for Correcting Systematic Undervaluation in African Sovereign Creditworthiness Assessment

detail.title: Sovereign Asset Party: An Analytical Framework for Correcting Systematic Undervaluation in African Sovereign Creditworthiness Assessment

keywords: The Ndege Group® Thought Leadership Series Classification: Working Paper / Policy Instrument Sovereign Debt

detail.abstract:
Africa holds $29.5 trillion in verified mineral reserves against $1.152 trillion in external sovereign debt. The ratio of minerals alone to total external obligations is 25.6 to 1. When all verifiable sovereign asset classes are incorporated, including agricultural land, Exclusive Economic Zone resources, and freshwater endowments, the Sovereign Asset Parity Index (SAPI) yields a continental score of 33.7, indicating that the continent is more than thirty-three times collateralised against its external sovereign obligations. 

The standard creditworthiness frameworks applied to African sovereigns by the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, and the three principal credit rating agencies compute this ratio nowhere. This paper introduces the Sovereign Asset Parity Index (SAPI) and the Mineral-Adjusted Creditworthiness Assessment (MACA) as corrective instruments for this documented omission. The SAPI measures the ratio of total verified sovereign asset value to total external sovereign debt. The MACA incorporates the SAPI as its primary domain within a composite creditworthiness framework alongside conventional debt service, revenue diversification, and institutional capacity metrics, producing an adjusted credit score applicable across all 54 African states. 

Both instruments are proposed as analytical inputs for the African Sovereign Development Finance Fund© (ASDFF©), the continental capital vehicle operating under the African Federation Treaty Framework© (Amayo, 2026a), with OmniGaza® providing the evidentiary and transactional substrate (Amayo, 2025b). Together, the AFTF©, the SAPI, the MACA, the ASDFF©, and OmniGaza® constitute a cohesive institutional ecosystem in which the SAPI and MACA provide the analytical basis for a continental sovereign finance architecture that reflects what Africa owns. Countrylevel SAPI scores are presented for 49 African states, and the complete African Sovereign Debt Cartography, covering all 55 AU member territories, is reproduced in full from the companion article, The Debt Cartography (Amayo, 2026b), as the primary evidentiary table on which this paper's analytical framework rests.

title: Your Enemy's Friend Can Be Your Friend: Borrowing from A Competitor's Bank
affiliations: American University of Sharjah

detail.title: Your Enemy's Friend Can Be Your Friend: Borrowing from A Competitor's Bank
detail.abstract: Forty percent of firms share banks with their competitors in the syndicated loan market. Firms borrowing from and switching to their competitors' banks pay lower loan spreads. The impact is stronger when firms are more financially constrained, bank monitoring is less costly, or product market is more competitive. When bank monitoring prevails after covenant violations, firms borrowing from competitors' banks experience greater sales growth, especially in industries with fiercer competition. The findings support Bolton and Scharfstein (1990) and suggest that borrowing from a competitor's bank is optimal-it not only mitigates managerial incentive problems but also deters product market predation.

title: Entrepreneurial Role Models and Entrepreneurship Education: Shaping Entrepreneurial Intentions and Aspirations in China
affiliations: Skills Academia Research & Insights Collective for Excellence

detail.title: Entrepreneurial Role Models and Entrepreneurship Education: Shaping Entrepreneurial Intentions and Aspirations in China
detail.abstract:
Purpose:

Although entrepreneurial intentions have been widely studied, much of the literature is grounded in Western contexts.

Comparatively less attention has been given to how local entrepreneurial role models and entrepreneurship education shape entrepreneurial aspiration and intention in China.

This review integrates insights from Social Learning Theory, the Motivational Theory of Role Modeling, the Theory of Planned Behavior, and Self-Determination Theory to interpret how exposure to local entrepreneurial ecosystems shapes attitudes, perceived feasibility, and motivational foundations of entrepreneurial action.

title: Neoscholeism Productivity Theory Human Risk Allocation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Neoscholeism Productivity Theory Human Risk Allocation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract:
Conventional economic theory views redistributive policies as involving an inevitable trade-off between equity and efficiency. While transfers improve social welfare, they are assumed to reduce aggregate output by weakening labor-market incentives. The Neoscholeism Productivity Theory proposes a radically different framework for economies shaped by Artificial Intelligence. As AI assumes a growing share of routine cognitive tasks, society’s primary binding constraint shifts from producing physical output to allocating human talent toward activities requiring original judgment, scientific discovery, and high-risk entrepreneurship.

This paper demonstrates that the Universal Dividend (D) functions not merely as a redistributive transfer, but as a critical macroeconomic risk-allocation institution. Using an occupational-choice model under Constant Relative Risk Aversion (CRRA) preferences, we show that an unconditional income floor generates two competing mechanisms: an Innovation Effect (Φ'(D) > 0), which encourages entry into high-variance pursuits by mitigating downside risk, and a Labor Supply Effect, which reduces conventional work hours.

Crucially, by introducing an Abundance Correction factor (1 - σAI(t)), we show that as AI task-substitution advances   (σAI(t) ⇾ 1), the marginal efficiency penalty of reduced conventional labor supply progressively vanishes. Weshow the existence of a unique, time-dependent interior optimum, D*(t), at which aggregate productivity is maximized. Consequently, the optimal Universal Dividend dynamically expands alongside AI penetration (dD*(t) / dσAI(t) > 0), serving as a dynamic efficiency mechanism that continuously realigns human capital with the frontier of innovation in an Age of Abundance.

title: The Capital Markets Supervisory Framework: Balancing Centralization and Proximity to Supervised Entities
affiliations: LUISS Guido Carli University

detail.title: The Capital Markets Supervisory Framework: Balancing Centralization and Proximity to Supervised Entities
detail.abstract: To address the reform of the European capital market in a direct and timely manner - particularly in light of the persistent fragmentation among national systems and the evident shortcomings of the current integration process - I consider the reform of supervisory mechanisms to be of central importance. In essence, this contribution aims to explore solutions that would restore a meaningful role to national authorities, with a view to understanding whether such a role can represent an essential condition for forcing the alignment of supervisory practices. Such a solution is, on the one hand, clearly consistent with the principle of subsidiarity and, on the other hand, does not contrast with the already existing EU financial supervisory framework. On the contrary, its aims to its enhancement and refinement. Emphasizing proximity features (to supervised entities) in the supervision framework may help accelerate the establishment of the Savings and Investments Union, which is now at the centre of the EU Agenda, and has been the subject of specific attention also in the Letta and Draghi Reports.

title: Google's AI & Economy ATLAS v1.0: Mapping Gemini Usage in the Economy
affiliations: , Google, Google, Google, , Google, University of Chicago - Booth School of Business, Google DeepMind, Google DeepMind, Google DeepMind, Google DeepMind, Google DeepMind, Google, Google, Google, Google, Google LLC and Google

detail.title: Google's AI & Economy ATLAS v1.0: Mapping Gemini Usage in the Economy
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the AI & Economy ATLAS (Activity, Task, Landscape, and Adoption Study), an ongoing economic research initiative using Google AI usage data. The first iteration of ATLAS is built on 15 million de-identified interactions across the Gemini App, Google AI Mode, and Gemini API. Using privacy-preserving algorithms as well as established and bespoke classification methods, we map AI usage to over 800 occupations, 4000 tasks, 300 household activities, 150 countries, and 140 languages. We then make a number of observations on what the data reveals about AI's diffusion, and its usage at work and in day-today life. In the workplace, we show that while AI adoption spans occupations covering just above 88% of US employment, penetration remains shallow and overwhelmingly collaborative in nature, with end-to-end task automation limited in scope. Outside of work, AI spans activities making up about 98% of Americans' non-sleep time, with disproportionately high use in high-friction tasks such as engaging with government and professional service providers, likely delivering economic value that standard national accounts may miss. Globally, adoption scales with national wealth and has broad linguistic distribution, with English queries representing only around a third of volume. As we build upon ATLAS and expand its scope and capabilities, we will continue to provide large-scale empirical evidence to inform the public, policy and academic questions about the ongoing AI transformation.

title: Stablecoin Adoption in Emerging Markets: A TAM-Based Model of Digital Finance Use

detail.title: Stablecoin Adoption in Emerging Markets: A TAM-Based Model of Digital Finance Use
detail.abstract:
Stablecoins have moved beyond the speculative niche of crypto-assets and now operate as instruments of everyday digital finance, with emerging markets serving as their primary environment of use. However, while existing technology acceptance frameworks explain how users form the intention to adopt financial solutions, they overlook the economic pressure under which stablecoins are actually employed. 

This study therefore examines and shows how the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) can be extended to explain stablecoin adoption under such conditions. The conceptual model was developed through integrative literature synthesis and theory adaptation, drawing on a final corpus of 73 academic, foundational, and contextual sources selected against predefined criteria. 

The synthesis identified seven determinant categories and assigned each of them a distinct function within the adoption sequence. Digital and financial literacy act as preconditions of evaluation. Macroeconomic necessity and infrastructural voids shape perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, respectively. Trust, informal credit systems and the intention-use gap determine whether declared intention becomes regular financial behavior, which positions actual use rather than intention as the endpoint of the model. Nine propositions specify these relationships for empirical testing. 

The model's contribution lies in organizing the determinants by their role in the adoption sequence and treating actual use as its endpoint. It also supports adoption-readiness assessment by fintech firms, banks, payment providers, and regulators.

title: Institutional Synchronization Theory: A Framework for Market Dynamics under Common Institutional Constraints

detail.title: Institutional Synchronization Theory: A Framework for Market Dynamics under Common Institutional Constraints
detail.abstract: We develop Institutional Synchronization Theory (IST), an equilibrium framework in which market-wide synchronization arises endogenously as the consequence of institutional optimization under a common constraint. Heterogeneous institutions solve their own mean-variance problems but face the same regulatory environment. A change in the common constraint enters every institution's optimization problem through a shared gradient term, aligning individually optimal portfolio adjustments in direction and concentrating aggregate institutional demand. Market clearing translates this demand concentration into amplified price responses, elevated return comovement, and stronger cross-asset volatility transmission. We term the resulting equilibrium a synchronization equilibrium. The theory yields four chained predictions-institutional demand concentration, dynamic return correlation, volatility spillovers, and temporary liquidity deterioration-that we evaluate using the 2026 Korea Exchange trading halt cluster as a natural experiment. IST is the first component of a broader research program on Institutional Market Dynamics (IMD) that reinterprets comovement, spillovers, liquidity fragility, and price impact amplification as manifestations of a single underlying mechanism.

title: A Temporal Dynamics Framework and Methodology for Computationally Intensive Social Media Research
affiliations: University of Auckland Business School, University of Auckland Business School and University of Auckland Business School

detail.title: A Temporal Dynamics Framework and Methodology for Computationally Intensive Social Media Research
detail.abstract: The growing availability of expansive social media trace data (SMTD) offers researchers promising opportunities to create rich depictions of societal and social phenomena. Despite this potential, research analysing such data often struggles to construct novel theoretical insight. This paper argues that holistically incorporating temporality enhances data collection and data analysis, subsequently facilitating process theory construction from SMTD. Recommendations to integrate temporality are outlined in the proposed Temporal Dynamics Framework and Methodology (TDFM). We apply the TDFM to investigate the temporal dynamics of mental health discourse on Twitter (now X) across different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic, theoretically framed in the context of innate psychological needs satisfaction. The findings reveal dynamic shifts in social media use, indicating that different phases of the pandemic triggered changes in the needs motivating, and being motivated by, social media use. This illustrative case reflectively evaluates the TDFM's usefulness in contextualising SMTD collection, analytical strategies, and process theory construction by incorporating a dynamic perspective on time. The full paper is available at https://doi.org/10.1177/02683962241283051

title: Credit Surfaces and Economic Uncertainty
affiliations: Yale University and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Credit Surfaces and Economic Uncertainty

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: Finance & Economics Discussion Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: The Credit Surface along the leverage dimension gives the bond spread as a function of the loan-to-value ratio. Empirically, we show that uncertainty shocks typically increase spreads and steepen the credit surface, profoundly affecting the supply of credit. Theoretically, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the convexity of the credit surface, and for changes in the anticipated distribution of collateral prices that lead to steepening of the credit surface. Finally, we show that the credit surface itself fully reveals the entire distribution of collateral prices, thus providing a new and vivid language with which to describe uncertainty and stochastic orders. Credit surface steepening itself is a new stochastic order that may better capture our intuitive notion of more uncertainty.

title: Governing the Memory Layer of Enterprise AI: Control Rights, Reconstructability, and Governance Hysteresis
affiliations: and George Mason University

detail.title: Governing the Memory Layer of Enterprise AI: Control Rights, Reconstructability, and Governance Hysteresis
detail.abstract:
Firms increasingly obtain general artificial intelligence capability from external platforms while jointly
producing organization-specific memory through recurring use. This separation creates a governance
problem below the level of the whole AI solution: the provider of the general model, the controller of
authoritative memory, and the runtime operator need not be the same party. We develop a two-period
incomplete-contracting model in which a firm contributes contextual knowledge, a platform contributes
technical structuring, and governance-dependent use changes memory stock, firm specificity, deployment
embeddedness, and functional reconstructability. Three results follow. First, layered governance can be
efficient: the firm controls authoritative memory and migration rights while the platform continues to supply
the model and runtime. Second, integrated platform governance can be efficient at adoption yet expand use
enough to generate the firm-specific productive memory that makes layered governance efficient later, even
though platform governance induces less firm knowledge investment. Third, directional reconfiguration costs
separate the operating-efficient governance boundary from the governance structure that can be implemented
from an inherited architecture. Reconstructability moves the forward and reverse switching thresholds toward
the efficient boundary, whereas deployment embeddedness moves them apart. The analysis identifies a self-
transforming property of digital governance: an initial allocation of rights helps produce the characteristics of
the asset that will later be governed.

title: Schema Markup Adoption in Top-Ranking Personal Injury Law Firm Websites: A Structured Data Audit of 1,005 Google Page-1 Sites Across 50 US States

detail.title: Schema Markup Adoption in Top-Ranking Personal Injury Law Firm Websites: A Structured Data Audit of 1,005 Google Page-1 Sites Across 50 US States

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the Founder and CEO of Rank Brilliance, a Semantic SEO agency that provides search engine optimization services to clients across multiple verticals, including legal services. The research was conducted independently and does not involve any client data, proprietary engagements, or commercial partnerships with the 1005 personal injury law firm websites included in the study sample. All analyzed websites were selected through publicly available search engine results and directory listings. The author declares no other financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the findings reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or personally identifiable information. The research is based exclusively on publicly accessible website content, including HTML source code and structured data markup, collected through automated crawling in accordance with standard web research practices. No ethics approval was required as the study does not fall under the scope of human subjects research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was self-funded and conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Structured data markup on the open web has moved from a rich-snippet convenience to a load-bearing input for entity extraction, knowledge-graph onboarding, disambiguation, corroboration, and, increasingly, large-language-model context assembly. Personal injury (PI) law firms operate in a legal vertical characterized by high commercial intent and dense local competition. In this context, the practical question is whether the firms already winning Google Page 1 are using schema markup, and how completely they are using it. This study addresses that question through a targeted audit of 1,005 unique PI law firm websites ranking on the first page of Google Search for five core practice-area keywords (personal injury, car accident, truck accident, medical malpractice, and wrongful death) across the largest city in each of the 50 U.S. states plus Washington, D.C. For every domain we crawled the homepage plus up to four ranking practice-area pages, extracted all JSON-LD blocks, scored the implementation against a five-dimension Schema Completeness Index (SCI), and evaluated eligibility for ten Google Rich Results features. We find that 63.7% of top-ranking PI firm websites deploy some schema, yet only 35.3% use the industry-specific LegalService type and only 20.6% emit Person or Attorney schema for their lawyers. Only 4.7% ship an Organization payload complete enough to constitute a brand-quality entity declaration. Spearman rank correlation between SERP position and SCI is a weak but consistent-0.0581, and between rank and Rich Results feature count is-0.084: schema quality is a tiebreaker, not a primary lever, in this sample. We anchor the findings to Google and Microsoft patents and published research that establish structured data as the codified interface into entity recognition, knowledge-graph onboarding, and generative-answer surfaces, and offer a prioritized set of deployment recommendations for firms and their SEO teams.

title: The Harms of Large Language Model Misuse in the Creation of Destructive Capabilities: A Defensive Review of CBRN, Cyber, and Harmful-Content Risks

detail.title: The Harms of Large Language Model Misuse in the Creation of Destructive Capabilities: A Defensive Review of CBRN, Cyber, and Harmful-Content Risks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The author has no financial relationship with, or funding from, any of the organizations or model developers discussed in this paper (including OpenAI, Anthropic, RAND, or any government body), and no such relationship influenced the analysis or conclusions.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or the collection of any primary or personal data, and no ethics approval was required. It is a narrative review based entirely on publicly available published sources. The criminal and civil matters discussed in Section 10 draw solely on publicly available court filings and contemporaneous media reporting; all individuals named are presumed innocent, and all such matters are presented strictly as unproven allegations.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or funding from any agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was conducted independently by the author as unfunded scholarly work.

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have intensified a long-running debate over whether they meaningfully lower the barrier for actors seeking to build destructive capabilities across chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) weapons, offensive cyber operations, and the mass production of harmful or hateful content. This paper is a structured narrative review of the empirical evidence published between 2024 and early 2026. It argues that the resulting harm is real but uneven, and that it is best understood through the concept of marginal uplift, meaning the improvement a tool provides over a realistic baseline, rather than through raw model capability. Drawing on randomized red-team studies, developer-disclosed uplift trials, provider threat-intelligence reporting, and primary technical literature, the review reaches a domain-differentiated conclusion. For CBRN, current models have not been shown to provide reliable novel capability beyond existing resources, although disclosed uplift trials indicate a narrowing margin with each model generation. For offensive cyber and harmful-content generation, the uplift is more tangible and accelerating, principally by compressing time, lowering the skill floor, and industrializing volume. Recent criminal and civil cases further show conversational models being consulted in the commission of lethal violence, chiefly in operational and psychological roles rather than as sources of novel capability. The paper examines the principal defenses and their documented failure modes, contrasts the divergent governance approaches of the European Union and the United States as of mid-2026, and concludes that the dominant near-term harm is a model acting as a force multiplier on existing harmful knowledge rather than inventing new weapons, but a model acting as a force multiplier that renders existing harmful knowledge faster, cheaper, and more broadly accessible.

title: Moral Characters: Social Media and Elections in the US
affiliations: University of Padova, Department of Economics and Management, Wilfrid Laurier University and

detail.title: Moral Characters: Social Media and Elections in the US
detail.abstract: We study how politicians' adoption of social media, and the use of moral language, affect electoral returns. We compile a new dataset covering over 4,000 Twitter accounts and almost five million tweets by US House candidates over 2008-2018. We document several descriptive facts: social media use rises and falls with electoral cycles, politicians' use of moral rhetoric increased over the period of study, and moral rhetoric is strongly associated with higher social media engagement. Using a regression discontinuity design on close primary elections, we find that social media use by candidates has a positive but imprecisely estimated effect on vote shares. This effect is strongly heterogeneous depending on the use of moral rhetoric, and is large and statistically significant for candidates with above-median moral language use. A complementary design using only candidates with Twitter also reveals a causal effect of moral language on vote shares. We also document that relative to other social media features (negativity, out-group animosity, toxicity) moral rhetoric drives more positive engagement. Finally, we show that increased coverage from mainstream news media and campaign donations are important mechanisms.

title: Disruption Threshold: An Extension of Moore's Law
affiliations: and

detail.title: Disruption Threshold: An Extension of Moore's Law

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: NS
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding; it was conducted independently by the authors.

detail.abstract: We show that three well-established market dynamics-the experience (learning) curve, S-curve adoption, and price elasticity of demand-jointly produce a sharp threshold in any technology market. When the product of a technology's learning rate and the price elasticity of demand exceeds one, the system tips into a self-sustaining regime of exponential volume growth and exponential cost decline, independent of the market's specific parameters. Moore's Law emerges not as a property of semiconductors but as a universal attractor available to any technology that crosses this threshold. We derive the conditions under which the regime arises, persists, and ends-including margin capture by dominant players, regulatory caps on demand, resource scarcity, and use-case exhaustion-and extend the framework to multi-component technology stacks and platform architectures. Applied to artificial intelligence, the model dates the crossing of the threshold to 2023 and explains why sufficiently steep learning curves cause subscription revenue to collapse even as volumes grow, underlying the industry's monetization anxiety.

title: The Tool Is Not the Answer. The Tool Is the Problem

detail.title: The Tool Is Not the Answer. The Tool Is the Problem

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed in the enterprise software industry; this essay reflects personal observation and views, not those of any employer.

detail.abstract: Enterprise organizations have invested significantly in systems that record what happened: CRM platforms, ERP systems, warehouse management tools, business intelligence layers. None of these systems were designed to hold a decision record: the structured, provenance-tagged, bi-temporal account of what was chosen, by whom, under what authority, on what evidence, against what alternatives, and with what expected outcome. This gap is not a vendor failure. Nobody has named the decision as the unit worth preserving, and that absence is structural, not accidental. This essay introduces the concept of decision provenance as a first-class architectural requirement distinct from data lineage, knowledge management, process mining, and compliance audit trails. It formalizes decision time as a third temporal axis beyond the valid-time and transaction-time axes of ANSI SQL:2011 bi-temporal systems, argues that the infrastructure for decision provenance exists and is well understood but has been systematically applied one layer short of where it is needed, and establishes four falsifiable conditions under which the central claims of the essay would require revision. This is the first essay in a three-part practitioner series.

title: Is Attention to Ignorance Growing? A Data-Driven Look at Developments in Ignorance Studies in the Twenty-First Century

detail.title: Is Attention to Ignorance Growing? A Data-Driven Look at Developments in Ignorance Studies in the Twenty-First Century
detail.abstract: This paper asks whether academic and public attention to ignorance and its associated field of study (agnotology, or ignorance studies) grew during the first quarter of the twenty-first century. We draw on OpenAlex for the academic literature, after correcting for a false-positive rate in phrase matching and for a recent indexing anomaly in that database, and on Google Trends for public attention, using a shared scale for both search terms. The answer is yes. The combined share rose from a mean of 0.35 per million in 2005 to 2009 to 4.57 per million in 2020 to 2024, a statistically significant increase (Mann-Kendall trend test, τ = 0.843, p = 3.0 × 10⁻⁹). An independent Pettitt change-point test locates this structural break between 2011 and 2012 (rate ratio 13.6, 95% CI 7.0 to 26.5), three to four years before the Routledge International Handbook of Ignorance Studies appeared in 2015. A control series (misinformation studies and disinformation studies) shows that the ignorance/agnotology pairing led this wider research family, though this lead is no longer assured: between 2020 and 2025, relative to 2014 to 2019, the ignorance share grew 1.6-fold, while misinformation studies grew 20-fold and disinformation studies 42-fold. The paper concludes that this sustained growth, together with the field's documented interdisciplinary fragmentation, supports the case for greater coordination within the field.

title: Beyond Asimov: A Neo-asimovian Framework of AI Guardrail Laws for the Governance of Autonomous Systems

detail.title: Beyond Asimov: A Neo-asimovian Framework of AI Guardrail Laws for the Governance of Autonomous Systems
detail.abstract: Isaac Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics, formulated as literary devices in the 1940s, were never designed as enforceable policy instruments. This concept note proposes an original set of seven AI Guardrail Laws, a legally inflected, technically grounded, and ethically pluralistic successor to Asimov's framework. Unlike their predecessor, the proposed laws operate at the institutional level, governing the obligations of AI system designers, deploying organizations, and public regulators rather than the behavior of individual machines. The laws draw on four intellectual traditions: Kantian deontology, utilitarian harm calculus, Rawlsian distributional fairness, and Habermasian discourse ethics, and are designed to remain durable across successive generations of AI technology. This concept note is submitted to establish a timestamped public record of intellectual provenance for the proposed framework.

reference: Journal of Information Technology, Cybersecurity, and Artificial Intelligence, 2026, Volume 3, Issue 4,, Pages 15-29
title: When Everyone has the Same AI: Competitive Advantage for Startups under Generative AI Commoditization

detail.title: When Everyone has the Same AI: Competitive Advantage for Startups under Generative AI Commoditization

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Information Technology, Cybersecurity, and Artificial Intelligence, 2026, Volume 3, Issue 4,, Pages 15-29

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), delivered through general-purpose foundation models accessible on demand at low cost, has become available to firms of all sizes. This accessibility challenges the dominant view in which AI capability, built from scarce data, infrastructure, and talent, is a source of competitive advantage: when the same frontier capability can be rented by any firm, the model satisfies neither the rarity nor the inimitability conditions that the resource-based view requires of an advantage-conferring resource. This paper develops a conceptual framework explaining where competitive advantage resides once generative AI becomes, in effect, a shared utility. Engaging the precedent of the information-technology commoditization debate, it argues that generative AI differs in kind: it commoditizes capability rather than infrastructure, displacing advantage from the technology to the complements it cannot replicate. The paper names this regularity the advantage-relocation mechanism, the displacement of advantage, when a capability-like technology is commoditized, toward co-specialized complements such as proprietary data, domain judgment, customer relationships, and the orchestration capability that converts a common model into a distinctive value proposition. Integrating the resource-based view, complementary-assets theory, absorptive capacity, and dynamic capabilities, and stated at the level of the firm with resource-constrained startups as its sharpest boundary condition, the framework yields a set of falsifiable propositions concerning the relocation of advantage, the role of absorptive capacity in differentiating firms that use identical models, and the accelerated erosion of AI-derived advantage. It contributes a strategic account of competitive advantage under technological commoditization and an agenda for empirical testing.

title: The C-E-A Framework for AI Agents: Compliance, Efficacy, and Autonomy -A Case Illustration in Personalized Robotic Care

detail.title: The C-E-A Framework for AI Agents: Compliance, Efficacy, and Autonomy -A Case Illustration in Personalized Robotic Care

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: AI agents increasingly perceive, reason, and act with reduced human oversight, yet accurate reasoning alone says nothing about whether a specific candidate action is fit to deploy: whether it is legally and practically usable, whether it will actually help given real-world constraints, or how much independent action the agent should take before deferring to a person. This paper introduces the C-E-A framework (Compliance, Efficacy, Autonomy), which evaluates one candidate agent action at one decision point against three questions: is the action legally, medically, and practically permitted by everyone who holds standing authority over it (Compliance); will the action actually help right now, given real conditions, once a binary feasibility floor is cleared (Efficacy); and can the agent act independently while the person retains genuine, supported choice, bounded by a documented escalation ceiling and a hard red line against non-consensual physical action (Autonomy). This paper illustrates the framework using personalized robotic care for older adults as a case scenario, and reports the framework's own open tensions, including an unresolved conflict between a caregiver's standing permission and a capable person's stated preference.

reference: Columbia Public Law Research Paper Forthcoming
title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books
affiliations: Stony Brook University, Stony Brook University, Columbia University - Law School and University of Michigan, Ann Arbor

detail.title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books

publicationDetails.detailsText: Columbia Public Law Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: Columbia Law School, Public Law & Legal Theory Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Generative AI can produce book-length works of fiction at near-zero cost. These books are often dismissed as low-quality ``slop'' that buyers will ignore, and are assumed to carry little commercial weight. We test that assumption with full-text AI detection across 14,419 self-published genre-fiction books sold on Amazon from 2023 to 2026, matched to daily sales records through June 2026. None of these books disclose whether or not they contain AI-produced content. We find that books for which we detected substantial AI text ($>$ 25\%) make up a large share of the catalog but a smaller share of sales. Even so, they reach commercial scale, winning a growing share of sales over time and taking more of the scarce top-rank positions once held by books with no detected AI text. Over this period, the number of books with observed sales in a quarter grew 19.2-fold, while quarterly revenue grew only 8.9-fold. The market therefore added selling books faster than it added revenue, and revenue per selling book fell across most genres. Books with no AI text lose the most ground in genres with high AI diffusion, and most of all where Kindle Unlimited availability is high. Among top-selling books, those with substantial AI text draw on more distinctive language from existing books than do books with no AI text; for these books overlap rises with revenue, a gradient we do not detect for books with no AI text. Generative AI can thus reshape a creative market through scale rather than quality. Our results bear directly on the market-effect question at the center of the fair use defense to copyright infringement.

title: The Sminora Gap Across Modern Systems: Verified Ecosystem Architecture as a Universal Response to Structural Information Asymmetry in Unregulated Service Markets.
affiliations: and

detail.title: The Sminora Gap Across Modern Systems: Verified Ecosystem Architecture as a Universal Response to Structural Information Asymmetry in Unregulated Service Markets.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. The research is conducted independently under the auspices of Association SMINORA.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is conceptual, structural, and methodological in nature, involving no primary human subjects, clinical trials, or patient data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The work is self-funded as part of the SMINORA Research Series initiatives.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the SMINORA Gap framework-introduced in Minoretskaia (2026c) as the structural distance between declared and verifiable professional quality-to the broader landscape of unregulated service markets. It introduces a fourth dimension of the Gap: the Vibe Gap, defined as the structural distance between consumer-perceived satisfaction following service consumption and the independently verifiable quality of the process that produced it. Consumer satisfaction, the authors demonstrate, is not equivalent to process verification-and in unregulated markets, it has become the primary substitute for it. The paper introduces Verified Ecosystem Architecture (VEA) as the conceptual and operational framework through which the four-dimensional SMINORA Gap can be systematically closed across sectors, jurisdictions, and scales. VEA is defined as an open integration architecture in which a trusted verification layer-SMINORA EcoTech as its first and defining operational implementation-aggregates, validates, and publishes compliance signals accessible to any market participant at the point of decision. The paper further introduces the Universal Digital Identifier (UID) as the foundational element of VEA-the persistent, verifiable, globally unique identifier that anchors every professional's trust record across platforms, jurisdictions, and time. The paper concludes that VEA represents not merely a product architecture but an institutional category: to the authors' knowledge, the first voluntary digital verification infrastructure designed to function as a public trust layer across unregulated service economies at global scale.

title: Introducing the 'Sales Stack Shadow': Six Years of French B2B Sales Technology Evolution (2019-2025)

detail.title: Introducing the 'Sales Stack Shadow': Six Years of French B2B Sales Technology Evolution (2019-2025)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares the following affiliations relevant to this study: Faculty Lead at Euridis Business School (the institution from which the survey focus originate), Founder of Weesifi (a B2B sales consulting and training firm), Adjunct Lecturer at CNAM Pays de la Loire, and Sales Methodology Coach at the IMT-Atlantique incubator. Euridis work intern and alumni focus was authorized by Euridis Business School. The anonymized dataset and analysis script are publicly available to enable independent replication.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Survey respondents were informed of the research and pedagogical use of the collected data and consented to participation. All personal identifiers (email, name) were removed prior to analysis; the shared dataset contains no personal data under GDPR.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Between 2019 and 2025, French B2B sales functions underwent a rapid transformation of their technological tooling, driven by the combined effects of buyer journey digitalization and the disruptive arrival of generative AI from November 2022. The academic literature remains underdeveloped on three counts: fine-grained longitudinal measurement of this transformation at the individual level, transposition of the Shadow IT concept to the B2B sales field, and differentiated analysis of generative AI adoption by salespeople's professional status.

This study draws on a repeated cross-sectional longitudinal design covering 901 French salespeople surveyed over six consecutive years through four harmonized waves (2019-2021, 2022, 2023, 2024-2025). The design adopts an explicit bottom-up stance: salespeople in the field are surveyed directly rather than their managers, a necessary condition for observing unsanctioned tools. The Sales Stack Shadow concept is introduced and operationalized through the index Sales Stack Shadow = n_free / (n_free + n_paid).

Four findings emerge. First, the technological stack doubles in two years (from 2.40 to 4.96 declared tools; Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001). Second, the Sales Stack Shadow Index reaches 47.4% in the 2023 wave: nearly half of the tools used are free and unsanctioned. Third, work-study students import significantly more free tools than employed professionals (1.36 vs 0.95; Mann-Whitney p = 0.005). Fourth, 71.3% of salespeople use generative AI without formal training, with a clear differential favoring work-study students (42.6% trained vs 20.2%; chi-square p = 0.007).

The study extends Shadow IT to the B2B sales field with a reproducible metric and empirically documents the governance drift zone in the French context.

title: The BNPL Loyalty Paradox: Higher Customer Value but Lower Retailer Commitment
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: The BNPL Loyalty Paradox: Higher Customer Value but Lower Retailer Commitment
detail.abstract: Buy now, pay later (BNPL) services have become a prominent feature of digital retail, with annual transaction values projected to surpass USD 300 billion and adoption expected to extend to nearly one-third of retail consumers worldwide. Despite their rapid growth and immediate influence on purchasing and payment behaviour, limited evidence exists regarding how BNPL use affects customer lifetime value (CLV) and retailer switching over an extended period. Drawing on Customer Lifetime Value Theory and Habit Formation Theory, and using Mental Accounting Theory to explain how consumers separate the enjoyment of a purchase from its delayed financial cost, this study examines the long-term consequences of BNPL adoption. A preregistered field-based randomized controlled trial was conducted with 112,840 customers across three medium-to-large online general-merchandise retailers operating in the United Kingdom and Australia. Customer behaviour was observed over 24 months. Pareto/NBD and Gamma–Gamma models were used to estimate CLV, while two-stage least-squares interaction models supported causal identification. Retailer-switching behaviour was assessed using Cox proportional-hazards models. The results show that BNPL availability significantly improves predicted CLV, primarily by increasing purchase frequency rather than average transaction value. At the same time, BNPL-financed customers face lower continuity-related barriers to switching retailers.

title: Religious Upbringing and Adult Human Development: Longitudinal Evidence from 22 Study Sites

detail.title: Religious Upbringing and Adult Human Development: Longitudinal Evidence from 22 Study Sites
detail.abstract: Does religious upbringing shape adult human development, or do observed differences primarily reflect continued participation later in life? I study this question using three waves of the Global Flourishing Study, covering 202,898 adults across 21 countries and Hong Kong. The data link religious-service attendance around age 12 to detailed measures of childhood conditions, current religious activity, and repeated adult outcomes. Childhood attendance is associated with higher adult flourishing, health, meaning, relationships, character, and selected economic outcomes, although these differences narrow substantially after accounting for family background and parental religiosity. Life-course comparisons sharpen the interpretation. Adults whose frequent participation ended after childhood display no broad advantage, while adults who currently participate frequently have similar profiles whether or not they attended frequently as children. Continued participation from childhood is associated with a modest additional advantage in aggregate nonfinancial flourishing, health, relationships, and some economic outcomes. These activation contrasts retain the same sign across contemporaneous, prospective, and within-person specifications, but they are small relative to the broader gap associated with current participation and cannot be separated from selection into persistence or correlated recall of childhood attendance. Individual fixed-effects estimates further show that income and flourishing move together within person, but childhood religious formation does not systematically moderate this relationship. Thus, religion functions as a continuing life-course institution rather than an independently identified childhood treatment.

title: The Best Buy? From Global Evidence to Government Practice
affiliations: , ,  and University of Minnesota - Minneapolis

detail.title: The Best Buy? From Global Evidence to Government Practice
detail.abstract: Can governments translate evidence on "what works" into learning gains in public schools? Morocco combined targeted remediation and structured pedagogy (two approaches ranked as "great buys" by a global evidence panel) and delivered them through the existing public-school workforce in 626 schools. Using a pre-registered matched difference-in-differences design across 276 schools and 22,846 students, we estimate that the program increased scores on an independent assessment after one year by 0.90 standard deviations: 0.52 in Arabic, 1.30 in French, and 0.93 in mathematics. Administrative records also show higher grade promotion (1.7 percentage points), while enrollment, which is nearly universal, remained unchanged.
